PoseBone._: A pose bone is one bone of a character skeleton while you pose it; these settings move, bend and limit that bone.
PoseBone.location: Moves the bone away from its resting spot (X, Y, Z). Bigger numbers push it further along that axis.
PoseBone.scale: Makes the bone bigger or smaller on each axis. 1 is normal, below 1 shrinks it, above 1 stretches it.
PoseBone.rotation_quaternion: Turns the bone using four numbers (W, X, Y, Z). It never gets stuck (no gimbal lock), but is hard to type by hand.
PoseBone.rotation_axis_angle: Turns the bone by an angle around a chosen axis, like spinning a skewer. Used when rotation mode is Axis Angle.
PoseBone.rotation_euler: Turns the bone with three simple angles (X, Y, Z). Easy to understand and edit by hand.
PoseBone.rotation_mode: Picks which kind of rotation numbers the bone uses. The other modes' values are ignored.
PoseBone.bbone_rollin: Twists the start of a segmented (B-Bone) bone. Low or negative twists one way, high twists the other.
PoseBone.bbone_rollout: Twists the end of a segmented (B-Bone) bone, like wringing a towel from the far end.
PoseBone.bbone_curveinx: Bends the start of a B-Bone sideways along X. Higher values make a stronger curve.
PoseBone.bbone_curveinz: Bends the start of a B-Bone along Z (forward/back). Higher values make a stronger curve.
PoseBone.bbone_curveoutx: Bends the end of a B-Bone sideways along X. Higher values make a stronger curve.
PoseBone.bbone_curveoutz: Bends the end of a B-Bone along Z (forward/back). Higher values make a stronger curve.
PoseBone.bbone_easein: How long the curve handle at the start is. Longer handle = the bend stays smooth over more of the bone.
PoseBone.bbone_easeout: How long the curve handle at the end is. Longer handle = the bend stays smooth over more of the bone.
PoseBone.bbone_scalein: Thickness of the B-Bone at its start (X, Y, Z). Differs from the end to make a taper.
PoseBone.bbone_scaleout: Thickness of the B-Bone at its end (X, Y, Z). Differs from the start to make a taper.
PoseBone.matrix_basis: The bone's own move/turn/scale packed into one 4x4 grid of numbers, measured from its parent and rest pose.
PoseBone.matrix: The bone's final position in the scene as a 4x4 number grid, after constraints and drivers have done their work.
PoseBone.lock_ik_x: Stops the IK solver from turning this bone around X. Like a hinge that cannot swing that way.
PoseBone.lock_ik_y: Stops the IK solver from turning this bone around Y.
PoseBone.lock_ik_z: Stops the IK solver from turning this bone around Z.
PoseBone.use_ik_limit_x: Turns on a min/max angle range for X when IK moves the bone, like a knee that cannot bend backwards.
PoseBone.use_ik_limit_y: Turns on a min/max angle range for Y when IK moves the bone.
PoseBone.use_ik_limit_z: Turns on a min/max angle range for Z when IK moves the bone.
PoseBone.use_ik_rotation_control: Lets this bone's own rotation also act as a goal for the IK chain, not just the tip's position.
PoseBone.use_ik_linear_control: Lets this bone's size act as a goal for the IK chain. Only matters when IK stretching is on.
PoseBone.ik_min_x: Smallest angle allowed around X while IK limit is on. Lower = it may bend further backwards.
PoseBone.ik_max_x: Largest angle allowed around X while IK limit is on. Higher = it may bend further forwards.
PoseBone.ik_min_y: Smallest angle allowed around Y while IK limit is on.
PoseBone.ik_max_y: Largest angle allowed around Y while IK limit is on.
PoseBone.ik_min_z: Smallest angle allowed around Z while IK limit is on.
PoseBone.ik_max_z: Largest angle allowed around Z while IK limit is on.
PoseBone.ik_stiffness_x: How hard the bone resists turning around X in IK. 0 bends freely, 1 is almost rigid.
PoseBone.ik_stiffness_y: How hard the bone resists turning around Y in IK. 0 bends freely, 1 is almost rigid.
PoseBone.ik_stiffness_z: How hard the bone resists turning around Z in IK. 0 bends freely, 1 is almost rigid.
PoseBone.ik_stretch: How much IK may stretch this bone to reach a target. 0 keeps it rigid, 1 lets it stretch freely.
PoseBone.ik_rotation_weight: How strongly the IK chain tries to match this bone's rotation goal. Low ignores it, high obeys it.
PoseBone.ik_linear_weight: How strongly the IK chain tries to match this bone's size goal. Low ignores it, high obeys it.
PoseBone.custom_shape_scale_xyz: Resizes the custom shape drawn for this bone on each axis, so the control looks bigger or smaller.
PoseBone.custom_shape_translation: Slides the custom shape away from the bone's center so the control handle sits elsewhere.
PoseBone.custom_shape_rotation_euler: Turns the custom shape without turning the bone, to line the control up nicely.
PoseBone.use_transform_at_custom_shape: When on, moving or turning the bone uses the custom-shape helper's position and direction as its center.
PoseBone.use_transform_around_custom_shape: When on, the bone moves as if it were a child of the shape helper bone, which then works like a pivot.
PoseBone.use_custom_shape_bone_size: When on, the custom shape grows or shrinks with the bone length. Off keeps it a fixed size.
PoseBone.hide: Hides this bone in the viewport (it still works). It only stays visible in Edit Mode.
PoseBone.select: Marks this bone as selected in Pose Mode.
PoseBone.custom_shape_wire_width: How thick the lines of the custom shape look. Low is thin, high is bold.
PoseBone.lock_location: Stops the bone from being moved when you transform it. Handy to protect a finished pose.
PoseBone.lock_rotation: Stops the bone from being rotated when you transform it.
PoseBone.lock_rotation_w: Locks the angle (W) part of 4-number rotations so only the axis can change.
PoseBone.lock_rotations_4d: Lets you lock each of the four rotation numbers one by one, instead of locking rotation as a whole.
PoseBone.lock_scale: Stops the bone from being scaled when you transform it.
PoseBone.rotation_mode.QUATERNION: Four-number rotation that never locks up (no gimbal lock). Best for smooth, free turning.
PoseBone.rotation_mode.XYZ: Three angles applied in X, Y, Z order. Simple, but two axes can line up and get stuck (gimbal lock).
PoseBone.rotation_mode.XZY: Three angles applied in X, Z, Y order. Simple, but can suffer from gimbal lock.
PoseBone.rotation_mode.YXZ: Three angles applied in Y, X, Z order. Simple, but can suffer from gimbal lock.
PoseBone.rotation_mode.YZX: Three angles applied in Y, Z, X order. Simple, but can suffer from gimbal lock.
PoseBone.rotation_mode.ZXY: Three angles applied in Z, X, Y order. Simple, but can suffer from gimbal lock.
PoseBone.rotation_mode.ZYX: Three angles applied in Z, Y, X order. Simple, but can suffer from gimbal lock.
PoseBone.rotation_mode.AXIS_ANGLE: Turn by one angle around one chosen axis, like spinning around a stick.

Lattice._: A lattice is a cage of points around an object; moving the cage points bends and squishes whatever is inside.
Lattice.use_fake_user: Keeps this data in the file even if nothing uses it, so Blender does not delete it on save.
Lattice.use_extra_user: An internal flag saying an extra user holds this data. Mostly for developers, you can ignore it.
Lattice.is_runtime_data: Marks this data as temporary, so it will not be saved in the .blend file.
Lattice.tag: A hidden marker that tools use to flag data while they work. You do not need to touch it.
Lattice.points_u: How many cage points run left to right (U). More points give finer, smoother bending but are heavier.
Lattice.points_v: How many cage points run front to back (V). More points give finer control.
Lattice.points_w: How many cage points run bottom to top (W). More points give finer control.
Lattice.interpolation_type_u: How smoothly the object follows the cage points along U.
Lattice.interpolation_type_v: How smoothly the object follows the cage points along V.
Lattice.interpolation_type_w: How smoothly the object follows the cage points along W.
Lattice.use_outside: Shows and uses only the outer shell of cage points. Hides inner points, which makes big lattices easier to handle.
Lattice.vertex_group: Limits the lattice effect to parts of the object painted in this vertex group. Empty means the whole object is affected.
Lattice.interpolation_type_u.KEY_LINEAR: Straight lines between points. Sharp and simple.
Lattice.interpolation_type_u.KEY_CARDINAL: Smooth curve that passes through the points.
Lattice.interpolation_type_u.KEY_CATMULL_ROM: Smooth curve through the points, a bit tighter than Cardinal.
Lattice.interpolation_type_u.KEY_BSPLINE: Very smooth curve that flows near the points without touching them.
Lattice.interpolation_type_v.KEY_LINEAR: Straight lines between points. Sharp and simple.
Lattice.interpolation_type_v.KEY_CARDINAL: Smooth curve that passes through the points.
Lattice.interpolation_type_v.KEY_CATMULL_ROM: Smooth curve through the points, a bit tighter than Cardinal.
Lattice.interpolation_type_v.KEY_BSPLINE: Very smooth curve that flows near the points without touching them.
Lattice.interpolation_type_w.KEY_LINEAR: Straight lines between points. Sharp and simple.
Lattice.interpolation_type_w.KEY_CARDINAL: Smooth curve that passes through the points.
Lattice.interpolation_type_w.KEY_CATMULL_ROM: Smooth curve through the points, a bit tighter than Cardinal.
Lattice.interpolation_type_w.KEY_BSPLINE: Very smooth curve that flows near the points without touching them.

MetaBall._: Metaballs are blobby shapes that melt into each other when they get close, like drops of water or mercury.
MetaBall.use_fake_user: Keeps this data in the file even if nothing uses it, so Blender does not delete it on save.
MetaBall.use_extra_user: An internal flag saying an extra user holds this data. Mostly for developers, you can ignore it.
MetaBall.is_runtime_data: Marks this data as temporary, so it will not be saved in the .blend file.
MetaBall.tag: A hidden marker that tools use to flag data while they work. You do not need to touch it.
MetaBall.update_method: How often the blob surface is rebuilt while you edit it. Faster updates feel smoother but look rougher.
MetaBall.resolution: Detail of the blob surface in the viewport. Low is chunky and fast, high is smooth and slow.
MetaBall.render_resolution: Detail of the blob surface when rendering. Low is chunky, high is smooth but takes more time.
MetaBall.threshold: How much the blobs must overlap before they merge. Low merges easily into big blobs, high needs them very close.
MetaBall.use_auto_texspace: Lets Blender fit the texture area to the object automatically as it changes.
MetaBall.texspace_location: Where the texture area starts, so you can slide textures around the object.
MetaBall.texspace_size: How big the texture area is. Changes how big or small a texture looks on the object.
MetaBall.update_method.UPDATE_ALWAYS: Rebuilds the blob fully at every change. Looks best, can be slow.
MetaBall.update_method.HALFRES: Rebuilds the blob at half detail while editing. A good balance of speed and looks.
MetaBall.update_method.FAST: Rebuilds the blob without full polygons while editing. Quick but rough.
MetaBall.update_method.NEVER: Does not rebuild the blob while editing. Fastest, but you will not see changes live.

Volume._: A volume is a cloud-like 3D data file (smoke, fire, fog) that Blender can load and render.
Volume.use_fake_user: Keeps this data in the file even if nothing uses it, so Blender does not delete it on save.
Volume.use_extra_user: An internal flag saying an extra user holds this data. Mostly for developers, you can ignore it.
Volume.is_runtime_data: Marks this data as temporary, so it will not be saved in the .blend file.
Volume.tag: A hidden marker that tools use to flag data while they work. You do not need to touch it.
Volume.filepath: The location of the volume file (like a .vdb) on your computer that this Volume reads from.
Volume.is_sequence: Turn on when the volume is a series of files, one per frame, so it plays like an animation.
Volume.frame_start: The frame number where the file series begins. Used to line up the sequence with your timeline.
Volume.frame_duration: How many frames of the file series to use. Low plays a short piece, high plays more.
Volume.frame_offset: Shifts which file plays at each frame. Positive starts later in the series, negative starts earlier.
Volume.sequence_mode: What the volume does when your timeline goes outside the file series range.
Volume.velocity_grid: Name of the data layer inside the file that stores how fast the smoke moves. Used for motion blur.
Volume.velocity_unit: Tells Blender whether the speed numbers mean per second or per frame.
Volume.velocity_scale: Strength of the motion blur from the volume's movement. 0 is none, higher smears it more.
Volume.sequence_mode.CLIP: Shows nothing outside the chosen range of frames.
Volume.sequence_mode.EXTEND: Holds the first frame before the range and the last frame after it.
Volume.sequence_mode.REPEAT: Plays the series again and again from the start.
Volume.sequence_mode.PING_PONG: Plays forward, then backward, then forward again, like a yo-yo.
Volume.velocity_unit.SECOND: Speeds are measured as distance moved every second.
Volume.velocity_unit.FRAME: Speeds are measured as distance moved every frame.

Speaker._: A speaker is an object that plays a sound in 3D space, so it gets louder as you get closer.
Speaker.use_fake_user: Keeps this data in the file even if nothing uses it, so Blender does not delete it on save.
Speaker.use_extra_user: An internal flag saying an extra user holds this data. Mostly for developers, you can ignore it.
Speaker.is_runtime_data: Marks this data as temporary, so it will not be saved in the .blend file.
Speaker.tag: A hidden marker that tools use to flag data while they work. You do not need to touch it.
Speaker.muted: Turns the speaker off so it makes no sound.
Speaker.volume_max: The loudest the sound can ever get, even if you stand right next to it.
Speaker.volume_min: The quietest the sound can get, even if you are far away. 0 means it can fade to silence.
Speaker.distance_max: Past this distance the sound stops getting quieter. Low makes it fade out fast, high keeps it audible far away.
Speaker.distance_reference: The distance where the sound is at normal full volume. Closer is louder, farther is quieter.
Speaker.attenuation: How fast the sound fades with distance. Low fades slowly, high fades quickly.
Speaker.cone_angle_outer: Width of the outer sound cone in degrees. Outside this angle the sound drops to the outer cone volume.
Speaker.cone_angle_inner: Width of the inner sound cone in degrees. Inside this angle the sound is at full volume.
Speaker.cone_volume_outer: Volume outside the outer cone. 0 is silent behind the speaker, 1 is as loud as in front.
Speaker.volume: How loud the sound is. 0 is silent, 1 is normal, above 1 is louder.
Speaker.pitch: How high or low the sound plays. Below 1 is deeper and slower, above 1 is higher and faster.

LightProbe._: A light probe records the light in one spot of the scene so nearby objects can show realistic reflections and glow.
LightProbe.use_fake_user: Keeps this data in the file even if nothing uses it, so Blender does not delete it on save.
LightProbe.use_extra_user: An internal flag saying an extra user holds this data. Mostly for developers, you can ignore it.
LightProbe.is_runtime_data: Marks this data as temporary, so it will not be saved in the .blend file.
LightProbe.tag: A hidden marker that tools use to flag data while they work. You do not need to touch it.
LightProbe.clip_start: Nearest distance the probe sees. Things closer than this will not show in its reflections.
LightProbe.show_clip: Draws the clipping distances in the 3D view so you can see what the probe ignores.
LightProbe.show_influence: Draws the area the probe affects in the 3D view.
LightProbe.influence_distance: How far from the probe its effect reaches. Low covers a small area, high covers more.
LightProbe.visibility_buffer_bias: Old setting (deprecated). Fought self-shadowing errors. Not used in newer Blender versions.
LightProbe.visibility_bleed_bias: Old setting (deprecated). Reduced light leaking through shadows. Not used in newer Blender versions.
LightProbe.visibility_blur: Old setting (deprecated). Softened the probe's visibility shadows. Not used in newer Blender versions.
LightProbe.invert_visibility_collection: Old setting (deprecated). Flipped which collection the probe could see. Not used in newer versions.
LightProbe.show_data: Old name (deprecated) for showing what the probe captured. Use Display Data instead.
LightProbe.use_data_display: Shows the light information the probe collected right in the viewport, to debug lighting problems.
LightProbe.data_display_size: Size of the little preview spheres that show the probe's captured light. Low is small, high is big.

ToolSettings._: Scene-wide tool options: snapping, pivot point, proportional editing, auto keying, painting and selection behavior.
ToolSettings.use_auto_normalize: While weight painting, keeps all bone weights on a vertex adding up to 1.0, so painting one bone takes weight from the others.
ToolSettings.use_lock_relative: Shows weights as if locked groups did not exist, so the remaining groups still add up to a full 1.0.
ToolSettings.use_multipaint: Paints on all selected bones' weights at once while keeping their balance with each other.
ToolSettings.vertex_group_user: Shows which vertices have no weight, so you can spot forgotten areas in a weight paint.
ToolSettings.vertex_group_subset: Chooses which vertex groups are shown in the list while weight painting.
ToolSettings.uv_sculpt_lock_borders: Keeps the outer edge of UV islands in place while sculpting UVs, so the shape outline stays put.
ToolSettings.uv_sculpt_all_islands: The UV sculpt brush affects every island under it instead of just the one you started on.
ToolSettings.lock_object_mode: Only lets you select objects that are in the same mode as the active one, so you do not switch things by accident.
ToolSettings.workspace_tool_type: What clicking and dragging in the viewport does.
ToolSettings.use_proportional_edit: Moves nearby geometry along with what you move, fading out with distance. Great for soft, natural shapes.
ToolSettings.use_proportional_edit_objects: Same soft falloff, but for moving whole objects: nearby objects follow along.
ToolSettings.use_proportional_projected: Measures the falloff distance on your screen instead of in 3D space, so it depends on your viewing angle.
ToolSettings.use_proportional_connected: Only affects geometry that is physically linked to the selection, not other parts that happen to be close.
ToolSettings.use_proportional_action: Soft falloff when moving keyframes in the Dope Sheet, so nearby keys follow.
ToolSettings.use_proportional_fcurve: Soft falloff when moving points in the Graph Editor, so nearby keys follow.
ToolSettings.lock_markers: Stops timeline markers from being moved or edited by accident.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff: Shape of the fade for proportional editing: how quickly the effect drops with distance.
ToolSettings.proportional_size: Size of the proportional editing circle. Small affects a tight area, large affects a wide area.
ToolSettings.proportional_distance: Size of the proportional editing circle. Small affects a tight area, large affects a wide area.
ToolSettings.double_threshold: How close two vertices must be to merge automatically. Low merges only very close points, high merges farther ones.
ToolSettings.transform_pivot_point: The point that rotating and scaling happen around.
ToolSettings.use_transform_pivot_point_align: Transforms only the locations of objects, leaving their rotation and size alone.
ToolSettings.use_transform_data_origin: Moves only the object's origin point, while the shape stays exactly where it is.
ToolSettings.use_transform_skip_children: Moves the parent but leaves its children where they are.
ToolSettings.use_transform_correct_face_attributes: Keeps UVs and color data looking right on faces while you move geometry.
ToolSettings.use_transform_correct_keep_connected: While correcting face data, keeps data joined at a shared vertex merged together.
ToolSettings.use_mesh_automerge: Automatically welds vertices together when you move one onto another.
ToolSettings.use_mesh_automerge_and_split: When merging, also splits edges and faces where vertices land on them.
ToolSettings.use_snap: Turns snapping on. Moving things then jumps to grid points or geometry instead of sliding freely.
ToolSettings.use_snap_node: Turns snapping on for nodes in the node editor.
ToolSettings.use_snap_sequencer: Turns snapping on for strips in the video sequencer.
ToolSettings.use_snap_uv: Turns snapping on when moving UVs.
ToolSettings.use_snap_align_rotation: Turns the object to match the surface direction of the thing it snaps to.
ToolSettings.use_snap_grid_absolute: Snaps to fixed grid lines instead of moving in steps from where you started.
ToolSettings.snap_angle_increment_2d: Step size for rotating in 2D editors while snapping. Small gives fine steps, large gives big jumps.
ToolSettings.snap_angle_increment_2d_precision: Smaller rotation step used in 2D editors when you hold Shift for precision.
ToolSettings.snap_angle_increment_3d: Step size for rotating in the 3D viewport while snapping. Small gives fine steps, large gives big jumps.
ToolSettings.snap_angle_increment_3d_precision: Smaller rotation step used in the 3D viewport when you hold Shift for precision.
ToolSettings.snap_elements: What your moving item can stick to.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base: What the Snap Base (the point you grab with) can stick to.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_individual: How each selected item is placed onto a surface when moved individually.
ToolSettings.snap_face_nearest_steps: How many small steps a Face Nearest snap is split into. More steps follow curved surfaces better but are slower.
ToolSettings.use_snap_to_same_target: Only snaps to the surface the item was first near, so it does not jump to other surfaces. Face Nearest only.
ToolSettings.use_snap_anim: Turns on snapping when moving keyframes.
ToolSettings.use_snap_driver: Turns on snapping when moving keys in the Driver Editor.
ToolSettings.use_snap_time_absolute: Snaps keys to exact frames instead of moving them in whole steps from where they started.
ToolSettings.use_snap_driver_absolute: Snaps to whole values instead of stepping from the starting value.
ToolSettings.snap_anim_element: What keyframes snap to when moving.
ToolSettings.use_snap_playhead: Makes the playhead snap when you drag it along the timeline.
ToolSettings.snap_playhead_element: What the playhead snaps to when you scrub.
ToolSettings.snap_playhead_frame_step: Gap between frame snap points. 1 snaps to every frame, higher skips frames.
ToolSettings.snap_playhead_second_step: Gap between second snap points. 1 snaps to every second, higher skips seconds.
ToolSettings.playhead_snap_distance: How close in screen pixels the playhead must be to snap. Low needs precision, high snaps from farther away.
ToolSettings.snap_uv_element: What UVs snap to when moving.
ToolSettings.snap_target: Which part of your selection lands on the snap target.
ToolSettings.use_snap_peel_object: Treats each object as one whole piece when finding the center of its volume for snapping.
ToolSettings.use_snap_backface_culling: Ignores faces pointing away from you when snapping, so you only snap to what you can see.
ToolSettings.use_snap_self: In Edit Mode, allows snapping to the mesh you are editing itself.
ToolSettings.use_snap_edit: In Edit Mode, allows snapping to other objects that are also being edited.
ToolSettings.use_snap_nonedit: In Edit Mode, allows snapping to objects that are not in Edit Mode.
ToolSettings.use_snap_selectable: Only snaps to objects you are allowed to select, ignoring locked ones.
ToolSettings.plane_axis: Which axis new shapes are drawn along when placing a base with a tool.
ToolSettings.plane_axis_auto: Picks the closest axis automatically when placing objects. Placing on a surface overrides this.
ToolSettings.plane_depth: Where the first click of a placement tool lands.
ToolSettings.plane_orientation: How the new shape is rotated when you place it.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_tool: What a tool snaps to while you use it.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_draw_additive: A new frame starts with a copy of the strokes from the previous frame instead of empty.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_draw_onback: New strokes go underneath the existing strokes in the layer.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_thumbnail_list: Shows the color list as a compact text list instead of big thumbnails.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_weight_data_add: Adds vertex-group weight data to new strokes using the current group and weight.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_automerge_strokes: Joins a new stroke to nearby earlier strokes in the same layer.
ToolSettings.gpencil_stroke_placement_view3d: Where strokes are placed in 3D space when you draw in the viewport.
ToolSettings.gpencil_stroke_snap_mode: Which points of a new stroke snap to the placement target.
ToolSettings.gpencil_surface_offset: Distance a stroke floats above the surface it is drawn on. Low sits close, high floats higher.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_project_only_selected: Strokes are projected only onto selected objects.
ToolSettings.gpencil_selectmode_edit: What gets selected when you click in Grease Pencil edit mode.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_select_mask_point: Sculpting only affects selected stroke points.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_select_mask_segment: Sculpting only affects selected points between other strokes.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_vertex_select_mask_point: Painting only affects selected stroke points.
ToolSettings.use_gpencil_vertex_select_mask_segment: Painting only affects selected points between other strokes.
ToolSettings.use_grease_pencil_multi_frame_editing: Edits several Grease Pencil frames at once instead of just the current one.
ToolSettings.annotation_stroke_placement_view2d: Where annotation drawings stick in 2D editors.
ToolSettings.annotation_stroke_placement_view3d: How annotation strokes are placed in 3D space.
ToolSettings.use_annotation_stroke_endpoints: Only the first and last parts of the stroke are used for snapping.
ToolSettings.use_annotation_project_only_selected: Annotation strokes are projected only onto selected objects.
ToolSettings.annotation_thickness: Line thickness of annotation strokes. Low is thin, high is bold.
ToolSettings.use_keyframe_insert_auto: Auto Keying: changes you make to a property automatically get a keyframe. Handy, but easy to key by accident.
ToolSettings.auto_keying_mode: Rules for when auto keying may add keyframes.
ToolSettings.use_record_with_nla: Each recording pass creates a new NLA track and strip, so you do not overwrite earlier work.
ToolSettings.use_keyframe_insert_keyingset: Auto keying only keys the properties in the active Keying Set.
ToolSettings.use_keyframe_cycle_aware: For looping animation, keys inserted outside the loop are moved back into the cycle range.
ToolSettings.keyframe_type: The look and meaning of new keyframes. Mostly a labeling tool for you.
ToolSettings.anim_mirror_bone: The bone used as the mirror reference when mirroring a pose.
ToolSettings.anim_fix_to_cam_use_loc: Fix to Camera creates location keyframes.
ToolSettings.anim_fix_to_cam_use_rot: Fix to Camera creates rotation keyframes.
ToolSettings.anim_fix_to_cam_use_scale: Fix to Camera creates scale keyframes.
ToolSettings.uv_select_mode: What you select in the UV editor.
ToolSettings.uv_sticky_select_mode: How selection spreads between UV points that belong together.
ToolSettings.use_uv_select_sync: Keeps your UV selection and your 3D mesh selection matched.
ToolSettings.use_uv_select_island: Clicking selects a whole UV island instead of one piece.
ToolSettings.show_uv_local_view: Shows only the faces that use the image displayed in the editor.
ToolSettings.use_uv_custom_region: Uses a custom UV area instead of the default 0 to 1 square.
ToolSettings.mesh_select_mode: Whether you select vertices, edges or faces in Edit Mode.
ToolSettings.vertex_group_weight: The weight given when you assign vertices to a group. 0 means no influence, 1 means full influence.
ToolSettings.use_edge_path_live_unwrap: Re-unwraps the UVs immediately when you change seams, so you see the result right away.
ToolSettings.normal_vector: The direction used when you copy, add or multiply normals in custom normal editing.
ToolSettings.vertex_group_user.ACTIVE: Highlights vertices that have no weight in the active vertex group.
ToolSettings.vertex_group_user.ALL: Highlights vertices that have no weight in any group at all.
ToolSettings.vertex_group_subset.BONE_DEFORM: Shows only groups linked to bones that deform the mesh.
ToolSettings.vertex_group_subset.OTHER_DEFORM: Shows only groups linked to bones that do not deform the mesh, plus non-bone groups.
ToolSettings.workspace_tool_type.DEFAULT: Dragging uses the tool you picked in the toolbar.
ToolSettings.workspace_tool_type.FALLBACK: Dragging does a normal selection box instead.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.SMOOTH: Gentle, rounded fade. A good all-round choice.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.SPHERE: Fade shaped like a round ball, staying strong in the middle then dropping fast.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.ROOT: Stays strong further out, giving a more pointed, rounder dome.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.INVERSE_SQUARE: Strong near the center and drops off quickly, like a spike.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.SHARP: Pointy peak that makes sharp, spiky results.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.LINEAR: Drops at an even speed, like a cone.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.CONSTANT: No fade at all: everything inside the circle moves equally.
ToolSettings.proportional_edit_falloff.RANDOM: Gives each point a random strength for a rough, noisy look.
ToolSettings.transform_pivot_point.BOUNDING_BOX_CENTE: Pivots around the center of the box that surrounds your selection.
ToolSettings.transform_pivot_point.CURSOR: Pivots around the 3D cursor, wherever you put it.
ToolSettings.transform_pivot_point.INDIVIDUAL_ORIGINS: Each selected item rotates or scales around its own center.
ToolSettings.transform_pivot_point.MEDIAN_POINT: Pivots around the average position of everything selected.
ToolSettings.transform_pivot_point.ACTIVE_ELEMENT: Pivots around the active (last selected) item.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.INCREMENT: Jumps in even steps from the starting position.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.GRID: Snaps to the grid lines of the viewport.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.VERTEX: Snaps to corner points of other geometry.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.FACE: Snaps onto the surface of faces, projected from your view.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.VOLUME: Snaps to the inside of an object, to its volume.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.EDGE_MIDPOINT: Snaps to the middle of an edge.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.EDGE_PERPENDICULAR: Snaps to the point on an edge nearest to you, forming a right angle.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.FACE_MIDPOINT: Snaps to the center of a face.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.FACE_PROJECT: Snaps by projecting onto faces along your view.
ToolSettings.snap_elements.FACE_NEAREST: Snaps to the closest point on any face.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base.INCREMENT: Jumps in even steps from the starting position.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base.GRID: Snaps to the grid lines of the viewport.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base.FACE: Snaps onto the surface of faces, projected from your view.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base.VOLUME: Snaps to the inside of an object.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base.EDGE_MIDPOINT: Snaps to the middle of an edge.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base.EDGE_PERPENDICULAR: Snaps to the point on an edge nearest to you, forming a right angle.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_base.FACE_MIDPOINT: Snaps to the center of a face.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_individual.FACE_PROJECT: Projects each item onto faces along your view.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_individual.FACE_NEAREST: Places each item at the closest point on a face.
ToolSettings.snap_anim_element.MARKER: Snaps to the nearest timeline marker.
ToolSettings.snap_playhead_element.Strip: Snaps to the edges of video strips.
ToolSettings.snap_uv_element.INCREMENT: Jumps in even grid steps from the starting spot.
ToolSettings.snap_uv_element.GRID: Snaps to the UV grid lines.
ToolSettings.snap_target.CLOSEST: The point of your selection closest to the target snaps on.
ToolSettings.snap_target.CENTER: The center of your selection snaps on.
ToolSettings.snap_target.MEDIAN: The average position of your selection snaps on.
ToolSettings.snap_target.ACTIVE: The active (last selected) item snaps on.
ToolSettings.plane_axis.X: The base is drawn on the plane facing the X axis.
ToolSettings.plane_axis.Y: The base is drawn on the plane facing the Y axis.
ToolSettings.plane_axis.Z: The base is drawn on the plane facing the Z axis (flat on the floor).
ToolSettings.plane_depth.SURFACE: Starts on the surface under the mouse, or the 3D cursor depth if none.
ToolSettings.plane_depth.CURSOR_PLANE: Starts on a point projected onto the plane through the 3D cursor.
ToolSettings.plane_depth.CURSOR_VIEW: Starts on a point projected onto the plane through the 3D cursor, facing your view.
ToolSettings.plane_orientation.SURFACE: Follows the direction of the surface you click on.
ToolSettings.snap_elements_tool.GEOMETRY: Snaps to any geometry in the scene.
ToolSettings.gpencil_stroke_placement_view3d.ORIGIN: Draws strokes at the object's origin.
ToolSettings.gpencil_stroke_placement_view3d.CURSOR: Draws strokes at the 3D cursor position.
ToolSettings.gpencil_stroke_placement_view3d.SURFACE: Sticks strokes to surfaces under the pen.
ToolSettings.gpencil_stroke_placement_view3d.STROKE: Sticks strokes to other existing strokes.
ToolSettings.gpencil_stroke_snap_mode.ENDS: First and last points snap and the middle follows between them.
ToolSettings.gpencil_selectmode_edit.SEGMENT: Selects the points between other strokes' crossings.
ToolSettings.annotation_stroke_placement_view2d.IMAGE: Strokes stick to the image and move with it.
ToolSettings.annotation_stroke_placement_view2d.VIEW: Strokes stick to the screen and stay put when you pan.
ToolSettings.annotation_stroke_placement_view3d.VIEW: Sticks strokes to your view, like drawing on glass.
ToolSettings.annotation_stroke_placement_view3d.SURFA: Sticks strokes to surfaces under the pen.
ToolSettings.auto_keying_mode.ADD_REPLACE_KEYS: Adds new keys and replaces existing ones when you change something.
ToolSettings.auto_keying_mode.REPLACE_KEYS: Only replaces keys that already exist, never makes new ones.
ToolSettings.keyframe_type.BREAKDOWN: A pose between main poses, for the movement between them.
ToolSettings.keyframe_type.MOVING_HOLD: A key that is part of a held pose with slight motion.
ToolSettings.keyframe_type.EXTREME: An extreme pose or other important spot, marked as you like.
ToolSettings.keyframe_type.JITTER: A filler or baked key, used for keying every frame.
ToolSettings.keyframe_type.GENERATED: A key made automatically by a tool, not by hand.
ToolSettings.uv_sticky_select_mode.DISABLED: Selects only the exact point you click.
ToolSettings.uv_sticky_select_mode.SHARED_LOCATION: Also selects UVs sitting at the same spot.
ToolSettings.uv_sticky_select_mode.SHARED_VERTEX: Also selects UVs from the same mesh vertex, even if apart.

UnifiedPaintSettings._: Settings shared by all paint and sculpt brushes, so size, strength and color stay the same when you switch brushes.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_unified_size: When on, every brush uses the same size instead of remembering its own.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_unified_strength: When on, every brush uses the same strength instead of remembering its own.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_unified_weight: When on, every brush uses the same weight instead of remembering its own.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_unified_color: When on, every brush uses the same color instead of remembering its own.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_unified_input_samples: When on, every brush shares the same stroke smoothing value.
UnifiedPaintSettings.size: Brush diameter in pixels. Small is for detail, large covers big areas.
UnifiedPaintSettings.unprojected_size: Brush diameter in real scene units instead of screen pixels, so it stays the same when you zoom.
UnifiedPaintSettings.strength: How strongly the brush acts on each dab. Low is subtle, high is heavy.
UnifiedPaintSettings.weight: The weight value painted into vertex groups. 0 is no influence, 1 is full influence.
UnifiedPaintSettings.secondary_color: The second color, used for the other mouse mode or when you flip colors.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_color_jitter: Randomly changes the paint color a little with each stroke for a natural, uneven look.
UnifiedPaintSettings.hue_jitter: How much the color shifts to other colors (hue). 0 stays the same, higher gives more varied colors.
UnifiedPaintSettings.saturation_jitter: How much the color strength (saturation) varies. 0 stays the same, higher mixes vivid and dull.
UnifiedPaintSettings.value_jitter: How much the brightness varies. 0 stays the same, higher mixes dark and light.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_stroke_random_hue: Picks one random hue per stroke instead of per dab.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_stroke_random_sat: Picks one random saturation per stroke instead of per dab.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_stroke_random_val: Picks one random brightness per stroke instead of per dab.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_random_press_hue: Pen pressure controls how much the hue randomness shows.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_random_press_sat: Pen pressure controls how much the saturation randomness shows.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_random_press_val: Pen pressure controls how much the brightness randomness shows.
UnifiedPaintSettings.input_samples: How many mouse positions are averaged to smooth a stroke. Low is shaky but responsive, high is smooth but laggy.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_locked_size: Whether brush size is measured on your screen or in the scene.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_locked_size.VIEW: Size is in screen pixels, so it looks the same however far you zoom.
UnifiedPaintSettings.use_locked_size.SCENE: Size is in scene units, so it grows and shrinks as you zoom.

Brush._: A brush is a saved tool preset for painting, sculpting or drawing, with its own size, strength, shape and behavior.
Brush.use_fake_user: Keeps this data in the file even if nothing uses it, so Blender does not delete it on save.
Brush.use_extra_user: An internal flag saying an extra user holds this data. Mostly for developers, you can ignore it.
Brush.is_runtime_data: Marks this data as temporary, so it will not be saved in the .blend file.
Brush.tag: A hidden marker that tools use to flag data while they work. You do not need to touch it.
Brush.blend: How the paint color mixes with what is already on the surface, like layer blend modes in photo editors.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type: Which sculpting tool this brush behaves like.
Brush.vertex_brush_type: Which vertex-color painting tool this brush behaves like.
Brush.weight_brush_type: Which weight-painting tool this brush behaves like.
Brush.image_brush_type: Which texture-painting tool this brush behaves like.
Brush.gpencil_brush_type: Which Grease Pencil drawing tool this brush is.
Brush.gpencil_vertex_brush_type: Which Grease Pencil vertex-color painting tool this brush is.
Brush.gpencil_sculpt_brush_type: Which Grease Pencil sculpt tool this brush is.
Brush.gpencil_weight_brush_type: Which Grease Pencil weight-painting tool this brush is.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type: Which hair-curve sculpting tool this brush is.
Brush.direction: Whether the brush adds its effect or does the opposite (Ctrl usually flips it).
Brush.stroke_method: How a stroke applies the brush as you drag.
Brush.sculpt_plane: The flat plane the brush uses as its reference when pushing or pulling.
Brush.curve_distance_falloff_preset: Shape of the brush falloff: how strength fades from the center to the edge.
Brush.elastic_deform_type: The kind of rubbery deformation used.
Brush.snake_hook_deform_type: How the snake hook pulls the surface.
Brush.plane_inversion_mode: What happens to the plane effect when inverted (Ctrl).
Brush.project_ray_direction_type: The direction vertices are projected in for Scene Project.
Brush.minimum_distance: Smallest gap kept between your mesh and other objects after projecting onto them. Low touches, high leaves a gap.
Brush.cloth_deform_type: How the cloth brush moves the fabric.
Brush.cloth_force_falloff_type: The shape of the area the cloth brush pushes with.
Brush.cloth_simulation_area_type: Which part of the mesh is simulated while you stroke.
Brush.boundary_falloff_type: How strength fades across a boundary (an edge of a mask or face set).
Brush.smooth_deform_type: How the smooth brush evens things out.
Brush.smear_deform_type: How the smear brush moves the surface.
Brush.slide_deform_type: How the slide brush moves the mesh lines.
Brush.boundary_deform_type: How the boundary brush deforms the edge area.
Brush.pose_deform_type: How the pose brush moves the segments.
Brush.pose_origin_type: How the pivot points for pose segments are set.
Brush.jitter_unit: Whether jitter distance is in screen pixels or relative to brush size.
Brush.falloff_shape: Whether the brush acts as a ball or a flat circle.
Brush.size: Brush diameter in pixels. Small for detail, large for broad areas.
Brush.unprojected_size: Brush diameter in scene units, so it stays the same size in the scene when you zoom.
Brush.input_samples: How many mouse positions are averaged to smooth a stroke. Low is responsive but shaky, high is smooth but laggy.
Brush.jitter: Randomly shifts each dab as a fraction of brush size. 0 is none, higher scatters them more.
Brush.jitter_absolute: Randomly shifts each dab by a number of pixels. 0 is none, higher scatters them more.
Brush.spacing: Gap between dabs as a percent of brush size. Low gives a smooth line, high gives separate dots.
Brush.grad_spacing: Distance before a gradient color cycle repeats. Low repeats quickly, high stretches the gradient.
Brush.use_color_jitter: Randomly changes the paint color a bit with each stroke for a natural look.
Brush.hue_jitter: How much the color type shifts randomly. 0 stays the same, higher is more varied.
Brush.saturation_jitter: How much the color intensity varies randomly. 0 stays the same, higher is more varied.
Brush.value_jitter: How much the brightness varies randomly. 0 stays the same, higher is more varied.
Brush.use_stroke_random_hue: Picks one random hue per stroke instead of per dab.
Brush.use_stroke_random_sat: Picks one random saturation per stroke instead of per dab.
Brush.use_stroke_random_val: Picks one random brightness per stroke instead of per dab.
Brush.use_random_press_hue: Pen pressure controls how strong the hue randomness is.
Brush.use_random_press_sat: Pen pressure controls how strong the saturation randomness is.
Brush.use_random_press_val: Pen pressure controls how strong the brightness randomness is.
Brush.smooth_stroke_radius: How far the cursor must move before the stroke follows. Low is responsive, high gives smoother, laggier lines.
Brush.smooth_stroke_factor: How strongly the stroke is smoothed. Low is loose and quick, high is very smooth but trails the cursor.
Brush.rate: Time between paint dabs in Airbrush mode. Low sprays fast, high sprays slowly.
Brush.color: The main paint color of this brush.
Brush.secondary_color: The second color, used when you flip colors or draw gradients.
Brush.weight: Weight value this brush paints into vertex groups. 0 means no influence, 1 means full.
Brush.strength: How strong each dab is. Low is subtle and builds slowly, high is heavy.
Brush.flow: How much paint is laid down per dab. Low is a thin build-up, high is thick and fast.
Brush.wet_mix: How much color the brush picks up from the surface. 0 stays clean, higher smears existing paint.
Brush.wet_persistence: How much picked-up paint stays on the brush. Low cleans quickly, high carries color a long way.
Brush.density: How many random elements (like hairs) the brush affects. Low touches a few, high touches many.
Brush.tip_scale_x: Stretches the brush tip along X. 1 is a round tip, lower or higher makes it oval.
Brush.use_hardness_pressure: Pen pressure changes how hard (sharp) the brush edge is.
Brush.invert_hardness_pressure: Flips the pressure effect on hardness, so harder pressing makes it softer.
Brush.use_flow_pressure: Pen pressure changes how much paint flows out.
Brush.invert_flow_pressure: Flips the pressure effect on flow, so harder pressing gives less paint.
Brush.use_wet_mix_pressure: Pen pressure changes how much surface color is picked up.
Brush.invert_wet_mix_pressure: Flips the pressure effect on wet mix.
Brush.use_wet_persistence_pressure: Pen pressure changes how long picked-up paint stays on the brush.
Brush.invert_wet_persistence_pressure: Flips the pressure effect on wet persistence.
Brush.use_density_pressure: Pen pressure changes how many elements are affected.
Brush.invert_density_pressure: Flips the pressure effect on density.
Brush.dash_ratio: Fraction of each dash cycle where the brush is on. Low gives short dashes, 1 draws a solid line.
Brush.dash_samples: Length of one dash cycle, measured in stroke samples. Low gives quick on/off, high gives long dashes.
Brush.plane_offset: Moves the working plane toward or away from the surface. Positive lifts it, negative sinks it.
Brush.plane_trim: Ignores vertices farther than this from the plane. Low limits the effect, high lets more vertices be affected.
Brush.height: How tall the brush effect can build, like the layer height of the Layer tool.
Brush.plane_depth: Max distance below the plane that is affected. Higher reaches deeper vertices.
Brush.plane_height: Max distance above the plane that is affected. Higher reaches higher vertices.
Brush.stabilize_normal: How steady the plane direction stays during a stroke. 0 follows the surface, 1 locks it.
Brush.stabilize_plane: How steady the plane center stays during a stroke. 0 follows the surface, 1 locks it.
Brush.texture_sample_bias: Number added to the texture values. Positive makes the texture stronger, negative weaker.
Brush.use_color_as_displacement: Treats each pixel color as a direction to push the surface, for vector displacement (Area plane only).
Brush.normal_weight: How much Grab pulls vertices out of the surface. 0 moves along your drag, higher pulls outward more.
Brush.elastic_deform_volume_preservation: How much volume is kept during elastic deformation. Low squishes freely, high keeps volume but can feel stiffer.
Brush.rake_factor: How much Grab follows the turning of your cursor path. 0 ignores it, higher turns the grabbed area with the stroke.
Brush.crease_pinch_factor: How much the Crease brush pulls points together. 0 only cuts in, higher pinches edges sharper.
Brush.pose_offset: Moves the pose pivot relative to brush size. Low keeps it near the brush, high puts it farther along the mesh.
Brush.disconnected_distance_max: Farthest distance to look for separate loose parts of the mesh. Low only finds nearby parts, high reaches farther.
Brush.boundary_offset: Moves the boundary pivot relative to brush size. Low keeps it close, high moves it away.
Brush.surface_smooth_shape_preservation: How much of the original shape stays when smoothing. Low smooths strongly, high keeps the form.
Brush.surface_smooth_current_vertex: How much each vertex's own position affects the result. Low smooths more, high keeps vertices closer to where they are.
Brush.surface_smooth_iterations: How many smoothing passes happen per brush step. More passes smooth more but cost speed.
Brush.multiplane_scrape_angle: Angle between the two scrape planes. Low gives a flat scrape, high makes a sharper ridge.
Brush.pose_smooth_iterations: Smoothing passes on the pose influence. More passes make a gentler bend between parts.
Brush.pose_ik_segments: How many bone-like segments the pose chain uses to bend the mesh. More segments allow more flexible bending.
Brush.tip_roundness: Roundness of the brush tip. 1 is a full circle, lower makes it more square.
Brush.cloth_mass: Weight of each cloth particle. Low is light and floaty, high is heavy.
Brush.cloth_damping: How much pushing forces spread through the cloth. Low lets it flop, high makes it stop moving quickly.
Brush.cloth_sim_limit: Extra distance past the brush where cloth simulates, relative to brush size. Low limits the effect, high reaches farther.
Brush.cloth_sim_falloff: Area over which the cloth effect fades out. Low is a hard edge, high is a soft fade.
Brush.cloth_constraint_softbody_strength: How much the cloth keeps its original shape, like a soft body. Low is floppy, high springs back.
Brush.hardness: Where the brush fade begins. Low fades from the center, high stays solid till near the edge.
Brush.auto_smooth_factor: Smooths each stroke automatically. 0 is none, higher gives a smoother result.
Brush.topology_rake_factor: Aligns mesh edges to your stroke direction for cleaner topology. 0 is off, higher is stronger.
Brush.tilt_strength_factor: How much pen tilt changes the brush strength. 0 ignores tilt, negative values reverse the effect.
Brush.normal_radius_factor: Size of the area used to find the surface direction, compared to brush size. Low is local, high averages a wider area.
Brush.area_radius_factor: Size of the area used to find the working plane, compared to brush size. Low follows tiny bumps, high is steadier.
Brush.wet_paint_radius_factor: Size of the area used to pick up color, compared to brush size. Low samples a small spot, high samples a wide area.
Brush.stencil_pos: Where the stencil image sits in the viewport.
Brush.stencil_dimension: How big the stencil image is in the viewport.
Brush.mask_stencil_pos: Where the mask stencil image sits in the viewport.
Brush.mask_stencil_dimension: How big the mask stencil image is in the viewport.
Brush.sharp_threshold: Detail below this level is not sharpened. Low sharpens almost everything, high sharpens only strong edges.
Brush.fill_threshold: Fill stops spreading where color difference passes this level. Low stops early, high spreads far.
Brush.blur_kernel_radius: Pixel radius used for soften and sharpen. Small is subtle, large is strong.
Brush.blur_mode: What kind of blur the soften brush uses.
Brush.falloff_angle: Angle where painting fades on faces turned from the view. Low fades early, high paints at sharper angles.
Brush.use_original_normal: When on, keeps using the surface direction from where the stroke started, even as you drag.
Brush.use_original_plane: When on, keeps using the plane from where the stroke started, even as you drag.
Brush.use_scene_spacing: Whether dab spacing follows the screen or the scene.
Brush.use_grab_active_vertex: Applies full grab strength to the active vertex rather than the cursor point.
Brush.use_grab_silhouette: Grab tries to affect only the outline shape of the object as seen from your view.
Brush.use_paint_antialiasing: Smooths the jagged edges of strokes.
Brush.use_multiplane_scrape_dynamic: The angle between planes changes during the stroke to match the surface under the cursor.
Brush.show_multiplane_scrape_planes_preview: Shows the scrape planes in the brush cursor while you stroke.
Brush.use_pose_ik_anchored: Keeps the last segment of the chain fixed in place.
Brush.use_pose_lock_rotation: Does not rotate the segment while scaling.
Brush.use_connected_only: Affects only mesh parts physically connected to where you start.
Brush.use_cloth_pin_simulation_boundary: Locks vertices at the edge of the simulation area to avoid glitches and tearing.
Brush.use_cloth_collision: The cloth collides with objects while simulating.
Brush.invert_to_scrape_fill: Inverting (Ctrl) uses the Scrape or Fill brush instead of reversing the displacement.
Brush.use_offset_pressure: Pen pressure changes the plane offset.
Brush.use_pressure_area_radius: Pen pressure changes the area radius.
Brush.use_pressure_size: Pen pressure changes the brush size.
Brush.use_pressure_masking: How pen pressure affects the texture influence.
Brush.use_inverse_smooth_pressure: Lighter pen pressure gives more smoothing.
Brush.use_plane_trim: Limits how far from the plane a vertex can be and still be affected.
Brush.use_frontface: Only affects vertices facing you, ignoring those on the back side.
Brush.use_frontface_falloff: Fades the brush influence on faces that turn away from you.
Brush.use_smooth_stroke: The brush lags behind the mouse and follows a smoother path.
Brush.use_persistent: Sculpts on a saved reference layer, so you can keep going back to the same base.
Brush.use_bidirectional: Projects vertices forward and backward along the direction, choosing the nearest hit.
Brush.use_accumulate: Dabs in the same stroke stack up, making the stroke stronger where it overlaps itself.
Brush.use_space_attenuation: Adjusts strength automatically so results look the same at different spacings.
Brush.use_adaptive_space: Spaces dabs by the surface angle instead of screen distance.
Brush.use_locked_size: Whether brush size is measured on screen or in the scene.
Brush.color_type: Whether you paint with one color or a gradient.
Brush.use_edge_to_edge: Drags the anchored brush from edge to edge instead of from the center.
Brush.use_alpha: When off, the transparency is kept as it is while painting.
Brush.gradient_stroke_mode: How the gradient moves along the stroke.
Brush.gradient_fill_mode: Shape of the gradient when using the fill.
Brush.use_primary_overlay: Shows the brush texture in the viewport.
Brush.use_secondary_overlay: Shows the mask texture in the viewport.
Brush.use_cursor_overlay: Shows the brush cursor in the viewport.
Brush.use_cursor_overlay_override: Hides the cursor overlay while you are stroking.
Brush.use_primary_overlay_override: Hides the texture overlay while you are stroking.
Brush.use_secondary_overlay_override: Hides the mask overlay while you are stroking.
Brush.use_paint_sculpt: Makes this brush available in Sculpt Mode.
Brush.use_paint_uv_sculpt: Makes this brush available in UV Sculpt.
Brush.use_paint_vertex: Makes this brush available in Vertex Paint.
Brush.use_paint_weight: Makes this brush available in Weight Paint.
Brush.use_paint_image: Makes this brush available in Texture Paint.
Brush.use_paint_grease_pencil: Makes this brush available when drawing with Grease Pencil.
Brush.use_vertex_grease_pencil: Makes this brush available in Grease Pencil vertex color mode.
Brush.use_paint_sculpt_curves: Makes this brush available when sculpting hair curves.
Brush.texture_overlay_alpha: How strong the texture overlay looks in the viewport. 0 is invisible, 100 is fully solid.
Brush.mask_overlay_alpha: How strong the mask overlay looks in the viewport. 0 is invisible, 100 is fully solid.
Brush.cursor_overlay_alpha: How strong the cursor overlay looks in the viewport. 0 is invisible, 100 is fully solid.
Brush.cursor_color_add: Color of the brush circle when adding.
Brush.cursor_color_subtract: Color of the brush circle when subtracting.
Brush.blend.MIX: Normal painting: the new color covers the old one.
Brush.blend.MUL: Multiplies colors, which always makes the result darker, like layering tinted glass.
Brush.blend.COLORBURN: Darkens and boosts contrast by burning the base color.
Brush.blend.LINEARBURN: Darkens by adding the colors and subtracting white. Strong, punchy dark result.
Brush.blend.SCREEN: Lightens the image, like projecting two slides on the same screen.
Brush.blend.COLORDODGE: Brightens and lowers contrast. Can blow out highlights.
Brush.blend.ADD: Adds the colors together, making things brighter and glowing.
Brush.blend.OVERLAY: Boosts contrast: darks get darker and lights get lighter, based on the base color.
Brush.blend.SOFTLIGHT: A gentle contrast boost, like shining a soft light on the surface.
Brush.blend.HARDLIGHT: A strong contrast boost, like shining a harsh spotlight.
Brush.blend.VIVIDLIGHT: A very strong contrast and color boost. Dramatic and intense.
Brush.blend.LINEARLIGHT: A strong light effect that brightens or darkens depending on the paint color.
Brush.blend.PINLIGHT: Replaces colors depending on how bright the paint is, for a patchy look.
Brush.blend.DIFFERENCE: Subtracts colors and shows the gap between them. Gives inverted, odd colors.
Brush.blend.EXCLUSION: Like Difference but softer and lower in contrast.
Brush.blend.SUB: Subtracts the paint color from the surface, making it darker.
Brush.blend.HUE: Keeps the surface brightness but takes the hue (color type) of the paint.
Brush.blend.SATURATION: Keeps the surface hue but takes the color intensity of the paint.
Brush.blend.COLOR: Applies the paint's hue and saturation but keeps the surface brightness.
Brush.blend.LUMINOSITY: Applies the paint's brightness but keeps the surface colors.
Brush.blend.ERASE_ALPHA: Erases the transparency, making painted areas see-through.
Brush.blend.ADD_ALPHA: Adds opacity, making see-through areas solid again.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.DRAW: Pushes the surface in or out, the basic sculpt brush.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.DRAW_SHARP: Like Draw but with a sharper, more defined edge.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.CLAY: Builds up material like adding clay, with a flat feel.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.CLAY_STRIPS: Builds clay in a flat strip shape, good for blocking out forms.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.CLAY_THUMB: Presses the surface like a thumb into clay, leaving a shallow dent.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.LAYER: Raises the surface up to a set height, like laying down a layer.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.INFLATE: Pushes points out along their surface direction, like blowing up a balloon.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.CREASE: Carves a sharp line in and pinches it, good for wrinkles and cuts.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.PLANE: Flattens the surface toward an average plane.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.MULTIPLANE_SCRAPE: Flattens using two planes at once, making crisp ridges.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.GRAB: Picks up a patch of surface and drags it, like pulling clay.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.ELASTIC_DEFORM: Stretches the surface like rubber for smooth, natural deformation.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.SNAKE_HOOK: Pulls out long tentacle-like shapes as you drag.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.THUMB: Pushes the surface sideways along the stroke, like smudging with a thumb.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.POSE: Bends part of the model like posing a limb, without a rig.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.NUDGE: Pushes the surface along the direction of the stroke.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.ROTATE: Twists the surface around the center of the brush.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.TOPOLOGY: Slides the edge flow of the mesh around so lines move without changing the shape.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.BOUNDARY: Deforms the edge of a mesh opening or a mask, face set or hole.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.SCENE_PROJECT: Projects the surface onto other objects in the scene.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.CLOTH: Simulates fabric reacting to the brush, for folds and drapes.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.SIMPLIFY: Removes small details to reduce mesh density.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.MASK: Paints a mask that protects areas from being sculpted.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.DRAW_FACE_SETS: Paints groups of faces (face sets) to organize and hide parts.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.DISPLACEMENT_ERASER: Removes multires detail you sculpted, going back to the base shape.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.DISPLACEMENT_SMEAR: Smears multires detail across the surface.
Brush.sculpt_brush_type.PAINT: Paints color directly onto the sculpt surface.
Brush.vertex_brush_type.AVERAGE: Replaces colors under the brush with their average.
Brush.vertex_brush_type.SMEAR: Drags colors along like smudging wet paint.
Brush.weight_brush_type.AVERAGE: Replaces weights under the brush with their average.
Brush.image_brush_type.SOFTEN: Blurs the image under the brush.
Brush.image_brush_type.SMEAR: Drags colors along like smudging wet paint.
Brush.image_brush_type.CLONE: Copies paint from another spot or image onto where you paint.
Brush.image_brush_type.FILL: Fills an area with the paint color.
Brush.image_brush_type.MASK: Paints a mask that hides or shows the texture.
Brush.gpencil_brush_type.FILL: Used to fill closed areas with color.
Brush.gpencil_vertex_brush_type.DRAW: Paints a color onto stroke points.
Brush.gpencil_vertex_brush_type.BLUR: Softens colors of neighboring stroke points.
Brush.gpencil_vertex_brush_type.AVERAGE: Smooths colors using the average under the brush.
Brush.gpencil_vertex_brush_type.REPLACE: Replaces the color of points that already have one.
Brush.gpencil_sculpt_brush_type.STRENGTH: Changes how strong (opaque) the stroke color is.
Brush.gpencil_sculpt_brush_type.GRAB: Moves the points under the brush as one group.
Brush.gpencil_sculpt_brush_type.PUSH: Pushes points aside, like combing hair.
Brush.gpencil_sculpt_brush_type.TWIST: Rotates points around the brush center.
Brush.gpencil_sculpt_brush_type.PINCH: Pulls points toward the brush center.
Brush.gpencil_sculpt_brush_type.CLONE: Pastes copies of strokes you stored on the clipboard.
Brush.gpencil_weight_brush_type.WEIGHT: Paints weight into the active vertex group.
Brush.gpencil_weight_brush_type.BLUR: Softens weights in the active vertex group.
Brush.gpencil_weight_brush_type.AVERAGE: Averages weights in the active vertex group.
Brush.gpencil_weight_brush_type.SMEAR: Smears weights in the active vertex group.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type.DENSITY: Adds or removes hairs to match a density.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type.COMB: Brushes the hairs in the stroke direction, like combing.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type.SNAKE_HOOK: Pulls hairs along with the brush as you drag.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type.PINCH: Gathers hairs together toward the brush center.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type.PUFF: Lifts hairs to stand upright from the surface.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type.SMOOTH: Straightens out kinks and curls in the hairs.
Brush.curves_sculpt_brush_type.SLIDE: Slides hair roots along the surface.
Brush.direction.ADD: The brush does its normal effect, such as raising the surface.
Brush.direction.SUBTRACT: The brush does the opposite effect, such as pushing the surface in.
Brush.stroke_method.DOTS: Places a dab at every mouse movement step.
Brush.stroke_method.DRAG_DOT: One dab you can drag around before letting go.
Brush.stroke_method.SPACE: Places dabs at fixed gaps, controlled by Spacing.
Brush.stroke_method.AIRBRUSH: Keeps applying paint while you hold the button, like a spray can.
Brush.stroke_method.ANCHORED: Fixes the brush center where you clicked and sets size and rotation by dragging.
Brush.stroke_method.LINE: Draws a straight line of dabs between two points.
Brush.stroke_method.CURVE: Draws along a curve you shape with handles, then confirm.
Brush.sculpt_plane.AREA: Plane follows the surface under the brush. The usual choice.
Brush.sculpt_plane.VIEW: Plane faces your view, parallel to the screen.
Brush.sculpt_plane.X: Plane is locked to the X axis.
Brush.sculpt_plane.Y: Plane is locked to the Y axis.
Brush.sculpt_plane.Z: Plane is locked to the Z axis.
Brush.mask_tool.SMOOTH: Blurs the edges of the existing mask.
Brush.curve_distance_falloff_preset.SMOOTHER: An even softer fade than Smooth.
Brush.curve_distance_falloff_preset.SPHERE: Round dome: strong in the middle and drops fast near the edge.
Brush.curve_distance_falloff_preset.ROOT: Stays strong longer, with a slight point at the center.
Brush.curve_distance_falloff_preset.LIN: Even fade in a straight line from center to edge.
Brush.curve_distance_falloff_preset.INVSQUARE: Very strong at the center and drops fast like a spike.
Brush.curve_distance_falloff_preset.CONSTANT: Same strength everywhere inside the brush circle.
Brush.deform_target.GEOMETRY: Moves the vertices of the mesh directly.
Brush.deform_target.CLOTH_SIM: Moves the cloth simulation constraints, so the cloth reacts and settles.
Brush.elastic_deform_type.GRAB: Grabs and drags the surface like soft rubber.
Brush.elastic_deform_type.GRAB_BISCALE: Grab with two scales of falloff, one big and one small.
Brush.elastic_deform_type.GRAB_TRISCALE: Grab with three scales of falloff, for very natural stretching.
Brush.elastic_deform_type.SCALE: Scales the surface bigger or smaller.
Brush.elastic_deform_type.TWIST: Twists the surface around the brush center.
Brush.snake_hook_deform_type.FALLOFF: Pulls with the brush falloff at the tip, making long strands.
Brush.snake_hook_deform_type.ELASTIC: Pulls the whole mesh with elastic deformation for a soft stretch.
Brush.plane_inversion_mode.INVERT_DISPLACEMENT: Pushes vertices away from the plane instead of toward it.
Brush.plane_inversion_mode.SWAP_DEPTH_AND_HEIG: Swaps the roles of the Height and Depth settings.
Brush.project_ray_direction_type.PLANE_NORMAL: Projects along the direction the plane faces.
Brush.cloth_deform_type.DRAG: Drags the cloth along with the stroke.
Brush.cloth_deform_type.PUSH: Pushes the cloth away from the brush.
Brush.cloth_deform_type.PINCH_POINT: Pulls the cloth toward a single point.
Brush.cloth_deform_type.PINCH_PERPENDICULAR: Pulls the cloth toward a line, making folds.
Brush.cloth_deform_type.GRAB: Grabs and holds a part of the cloth.
Brush.cloth_deform_type.EXPAND: Spreads the cloth outward from the brush center.
Brush.cloth_deform_type.SNAKE_HOOK: Pulls the cloth into long stretched shapes.
Brush.cloth_force_falloff_type.RADIAL: Force spreads out in a round circle from the brush center.
Brush.cloth_force_falloff_type.PLANE: Force acts across a flat plane.
Brush.cloth_simulation_area_type.LOCAL: Simulates only the area around the brush.
Brush.cloth_simulation_area_type.DYNAMIC: Simulates an area that moves along with the brush.
Brush.boundary_falloff_type.CONSTANT: Same deformation across the entire boundary.
Brush.boundary_falloff_type.RADIUS: Deformation only near the brush, fading with distance.
Brush.boundary_falloff_type.LOOP: Deformation repeats in a loop pattern along the boundary.
Brush.boundary_falloff_type.LOOP_INVERT: A loop pattern with the effect flipped.
Brush.smooth_deform_type.LAPLACIAN: Smooths both surface and volume, so shapes can shrink slightly.
Brush.smooth_deform_type.SURFACE: Smooths the surface while keeping the overall volume of the shape.
Brush.smear_deform_type.DRAG: Drags the surface along the stroke.
Brush.smear_deform_type.PINCH: Pulls the surface together toward the stroke.
Brush.smear_deform_type.EXPAND: Pushes the surface apart from the stroke.
Brush.slide_deform_type.DRAG: Drags mesh lines along the stroke.
Brush.boundary_deform_type.BEND: Bends the area around the boundary.
Brush.boundary_deform_type.GRAB: Grabs and drags the boundary area.
Brush.pose_deform_type.ROTATE_TWIST: Rotates and twists the part, like bending an arm.
Brush.pose_deform_type.SQUASH_STRETCH: Squashes or stretches the part like rubber.
Brush.pose_origin_type.TOPOLOGY: Finds pivot points automatically from the mesh shape.
Brush.pose_origin_type.FACE_SETS: Makes one segment per face set, using their shared edges as pivots.
Brush.pose_origin_type.FACE_SETS_FK: Simulates a bone chain (FK) using face sets for natural limb bending.
Brush.jitter_unit.VIEW: Jitter is measured in screen pixels.
Brush.jitter_unit.BRUSH: Jitter is measured relative to the brush size.
Brush.falloff_shape.SPHERE: Acts on everything inside a 3D ball around the brush center.
Brush.falloff_shape.PROJECTED: Acts on a flat circle projected through the model from your view, affecting front and back.
Brush.blur_mode.BOX: Even blur that treats all nearby pixels equally. Quick but slightly blocky.
Brush.blur_mode.GAUSSIAN: Smooth, natural blur that favors pixels near the center.
Brush.use_scene_spacing.VIEW: Spacing is measured on screen, relative to your view.
Brush.use_scene_spacing.SCENE: Spacing is measured in the scene, so it stays fixed while you zoom.
Brush.use_pressure_masking.NONE: Pressure does not affect the texture.
Brush.use_pressure_masking.RAMP: Harder pressure gradually reduces the texture's influence.
Brush.use_pressure_masking.CUTOFF: Pressure turns the texture off abruptly past a point.
Brush.use_locked_size.VIEW: Size is in screen pixels, so it stays the same when you zoom.
Brush.use_locked_size.SCENE: Size is in scene units, so it changes as you zoom.
Brush.color_type.GRADIENT: Paints with a gradient that blends between colors.
Brush.gradient_stroke_mode.PRESSURE: The gradient changes with pen pressure.
Brush.gradient_stroke_mode.SPACING_REPEAT: The gradient repeats again after each spacing length.
Brush.gradient_stroke_mode.SPACING_CLAMP: The gradient runs once and holds its last color.
Brush.gradient_fill_mode.LINEAR: Gradient runs in a straight line.
Brush.gradient_fill_mode.RADIAL: Gradient spreads out from a center point in a circle.

ImagePaint._: Settings for painting textures directly on a 3D model or an image.
ImagePaint.show_brush: Draws the brush circle on screen so you see where you will paint.
ImagePaint.show_brush_on_surface: Draws the brush circle hugging the surface of the model instead of flat on screen.
ImagePaint.show_low_resolution: For multires models, shows a lighter version while you move the view so navigation stays smooth.
ImagePaint.use_sculpt_delay_updates: Only updates geometry when it enters the view, which makes moving the view faster.
ImagePaint.show_bvh_nodes: Shows the hidden speed-up structure (BVH) as colored patches on the model. Mostly for debugging.
ImagePaint.use_symmetry_x: Mirrors your strokes across the X axis, so both sides get painted.
ImagePaint.use_symmetry_y: Mirrors your strokes across the Y axis.
ImagePaint.use_symmetry_z: Mirrors your strokes across the Z axis.
ImagePaint.use_symmetry_feather: Softens the brush where mirrored dabs overlap, to avoid doubled-up spots.
ImagePaint.use_cavity: Paints mainly in dents and crevices (or on ridges) depending on the shape of the mesh.
ImagePaint.tile_offset: Distance between copies of a tiled stroke. Low copies close together, high spreads them out.
ImagePaint.tile_x: Repeats your strokes along the X axis.
ImagePaint.tile_y: Repeats your strokes along the Y axis.
ImagePaint.tile_z: Repeats your strokes along the Z axis.
ImagePaint.show_strength_curve: Shows the curve that controls how pen pressure changes strength.
ImagePaint.show_size_curve: Shows the curve that controls how pen pressure changes size.
ImagePaint.show_jitter_curve: Shows the curve that controls how pen pressure changes jitter.
ImagePaint.use_occlude: Only paints faces directly under the brush, not ones hidden behind them. More accurate but slower.
ImagePaint.use_backface_culling: Skips faces turned away from you. Faster, and keeps you from painting the back by accident.
ImagePaint.use_normal_falloff: Paints strongest on faces pointing at you and weaker on faces turned away.
ImagePaint.use_stencil_layer: Uses the UV map layer buttons to choose which layer the stencil mask comes from.
ImagePaint.invert_stencil: Flips the stencil so the painted area becomes the protected area and the other way around.
ImagePaint.stencil_color: The color the stencil is drawn in on screen, so you can see it against your model.
ImagePaint.dither: Adds tiny noise when painting on 8-bit images to hide visible color banding. 0 is none, higher is more.
ImagePaint.use_clone_layer: Uses a second UV map as the clone source. If off, the 3D cursor is the source.
ImagePaint.seam_bleed: How many pixels the paint spills past UV edges to hide seams. Low may show lines, high is slower.
ImagePaint.normal_angle: Angle at which painting fades on faces turned from you. Low fades early, high lets you paint at sharper angles.
ImagePaint.screen_grab_size: Size of the screenshot taken when you re-project a view onto the model. Bigger is sharper but heavier.
ImagePaint.mode: Where projection painting gets its images from.
ImagePaint.interpolation: How the texture is sampled when painting.
ImagePaint.clone_alpha: How see-through the clone source image is shown. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
ImagePaint.clone_offset: Shifts the clone source image so you can line it up with where you paint.
ImagePaint.mode.MATERIAL: Finds the image slots from the object's material.
ImagePaint.mode.IMAGE: Paints on one image you pick directly.
ImagePaint.interpolation.LINEAR: Smooths between texture pixels for a softer look.
ImagePaint.interpolation.CLOSEST: Uses the nearest pixel with no smoothing, for a crisp pixel look.

Sculpt._: Settings for sculpting a 3D model like clay: symmetry, dynamic topology detail and brush display.
Sculpt.show_brush: Draws the brush circle on screen so you see where you will sculpt.
Sculpt.show_brush_on_surface: Draws the brush circle hugging the surface instead of flat on screen.
Sculpt.show_low_resolution: For multires models, shows a lighter version while you move the view so navigation stays smooth.
Sculpt.use_sculpt_delay_updates: Only updates geometry when it enters the view, which makes moving the view faster.
Sculpt.show_bvh_nodes: Shows the hidden speed-up structure (BVH) as colored patches on the model. Mostly for debugging.
Sculpt.use_symmetry_x: Mirrors your strokes across the X axis, so both sides are sculpted.
Sculpt.use_symmetry_y: Mirrors your strokes across the Y axis.
Sculpt.use_symmetry_z: Mirrors your strokes across the Z axis.
Sculpt.use_symmetry_feather: Softens the brush where mirrored dabs overlap, to avoid doubled-up spots.
Sculpt.use_cavity: Limits the brush to dents (or ridges) of the mesh using its shape.
Sculpt.tile_offset: Distance between copies of a tiled stroke. Low copies close together, high spreads them out.
Sculpt.tile_x: Repeats your strokes along the X axis.
Sculpt.tile_y: Repeats your strokes along the Y axis.
Sculpt.tile_z: Repeats your strokes along the Z axis.
Sculpt.show_strength_curve: Shows the curve that controls how pen pressure changes strength.
Sculpt.show_size_curve: Shows the curve that controls how pen pressure changes size.
Sculpt.show_jitter_curve: Shows the curve that controls how pen pressure changes jitter.
Sculpt.lock_x: Stops sculpting from moving vertices along the X axis.
Sculpt.lock_y: Stops sculpting from moving vertices along the Y axis.
Sculpt.lock_z: Stops sculpting from moving vertices along the Z axis.
Sculpt.use_deform_only: Shows only deform modifiers while sculpting and hides ones that add geometry, to keep the sculpt fast.
Sculpt.detail_size: Longest allowed edge for dynamic topology, in pixels. Low gives fine detail with many polygons, high gives coarse detail.
Sculpt.detail_percent: Longest allowed edge for dynamic topology as a percent of brush size. Low is finer, high is coarser.
Sculpt.constant_detail_resolution: Detail level in scene units. Higher numbers mean smaller edges, so more detail and more polygons.
Sculpt.symmetrize_direction: Which side copies onto the other when you use Symmetrize.
Sculpt.detail_refine_method: How dynamic topology adds or removes polygons while you sculpt.
Sculpt.detail_type_method: How the detail size is worked out in dynamic topology.
Sculpt.gravity: How much the sculpt gets pulled down after each dab. 0 is none, higher sags more.
Sculpt.transform_mode: How the Transform tool moves the part it affects.
Sculpt.symmetrize_direction.NEGATIVE_X: Copies the negative X side onto the positive X side.
Sculpt.symmetrize_direction.POSITIVE_X: Copies the positive X side onto the negative X side.
Sculpt.symmetrize_direction.NEGATIVE_Y: Copies the negative Y side onto the positive Y side.
Sculpt.symmetrize_direction.POSITIVE_Y: Copies the positive Y side onto the negative Y side.
Sculpt.symmetrize_direction.NEGATIVE_Z: Copies the negative Z side onto the positive Z side.
Sculpt.symmetrize_direction.POSITIVE_Z: Copies the positive Z side onto the negative Z side.
Sculpt.detail_refine_method.SUBDIVIDE: Splits long edges to add detail where you sculpt.
Sculpt.detail_refine_method.COLLAPSE: Merges short edges to remove detail where you sculpt.
Sculpt.detail_refine_method.SUBDIVIDE_COLLAPSE: Does both: splits long edges and merges short ones.
Sculpt.detail_type_method.RELATIVE: Detail depends on brush size and how zoomed in you are.
Sculpt.detail_type_method.CONSTANT: Detail is fixed in the scene, no matter how you zoom.
Sculpt.detail_type_method.BRUSH: Detail follows the brush size only.
Sculpt.detail_type_method.MANUAL: Detail does not change per stroke; you apply it yourself with a button.
Sculpt.transform_mode.ALL_VERTICES: Moves all vertices equally, like grabbing the whole thing.
Sculpt.transform_mode.RADIUS_ELASTIC: Moves the area under the brush with a soft, stretchy falloff, like rubber.

Keyframe._: A keyframe is a saved value at one moment in time; Blender fills in the motion between keyframes.
Keyframe.select_left_handle: Marks the left curve handle as selected, so you can move it in the Graph Editor.
Keyframe.select_right_handle: Marks the right curve handle as selected, so you can move it in the Graph Editor.
Keyframe.select_control_point: Marks the keyframe point itself as selected.
Keyframe.handle_left_type: How the left handle behaves. It shapes the curve coming into this key.
Keyframe.handle_right_type: How the right handle behaves. It shapes the curve leaving this key.
Keyframe.interpolation: How the value moves from this keyframe to the next one.
Keyframe.type: A label for the key. It does not change the animation, only how the key looks in the timeline.
Keyframe.easing: Which end of the segment between this and the next key uses the easing type. Only matters for easing interpolations.
Keyframe.back: How far Back easing overshoots the target. 0 means no overshoot, higher means a bigger overshoot before settling.
Keyframe.amplitude: How big the swings of Elastic easing are. Low is a small wobble, high is a big one.
Keyframe.period: Time between wobbles in Elastic easing. Low wobbles fast, high wobbles slowly.
Keyframe.handle_left: Position (frame and value) of the left handle, the one before the key.
Keyframe.co: Position of the keyframe itself: frame number and value.
Keyframe.co_ui: Position of the keyframe (frame and value). Changing it also moves the handles with it.
Keyframe.handle_right: Position (frame and value) of the right handle, the one after the key.
Keyframe.handle_left_type.FREE: Handle moves on its own, with no link to the other handle. Allows sharp corners.
Keyframe.handle_left_type.ALIGNED: Handle can be turned freely but stays in line with the other handle, keeping the curve smooth.
Keyframe.handle_left_type.VECTOR: Handle points toward the next or previous key, making straight lines.
Keyframe.handle_left_type.AUTO: Blender sets the handle for a smooth curve. It can overshoot slightly.
Keyframe.handle_left_type.AUTO_CLAMPED: Smooth automatic handle that never overshoots the key values. The default.
Keyframe.handle_right_type.FREE: Handle moves on its own, with no link to the other handle. Allows sharp corners.
Keyframe.handle_right_type.ALIGNED: Handle can be turned freely but stays in line with the other handle, keeping the curve smooth.
Keyframe.handle_right_type.VECTOR: Handle points toward the next or previous key, making straight lines.
Keyframe.handle_right_type.AUTO: Blender sets the handle for a smooth curve. It can overshoot slightly.
Keyframe.handle_right_type.AUTO_CLAMPED: Smooth automatic handle that never overshoots the key values. The default.
Keyframe.interpolation.CONSTANT: No in-between: the value stays the same, then jumps at the next key.
Keyframe.interpolation.LINEAR: Straight line at an even speed between the two keys.
Keyframe.interpolation.BEZIER: Smooth curve shaped by the handles. The standard choice.
Keyframe.interpolation.SINE: Gentle easing that is almost linear, the softest of the easing types.
Keyframe.interpolation.QUAD: Easing using a squared curve, a medium-soft start and stop.
