Keyframe.interpolation.CUBIC: Easing using a cubed curve, a stronger start and stop than Quad.
Keyframe.interpolation.QUART: Easing using a fourth-power curve, a very strong ease.
Keyframe.interpolation.QUINT: Easing using a fifth-power curve, an even stronger ease.
Keyframe.interpolation.EXPO: Exponential easing: very slow start or end then a fast change. Dramatic.
Keyframe.interpolation.CIRC: Circular easing: the strongest and most abrupt of the easing types.
Keyframe.interpolation.BACK: Overshoots past the target, then settles back into place.
Keyframe.interpolation.BOUNCE: Bounces like a ball landing, with smaller and smaller hops.
Keyframe.interpolation.ELASTIC: Wobbles like a spring, with a shrinking back-and-forth swing.
Keyframe.type.KEYFRAME: Normal key, used for main poses.
Keyframe.type.BREAKDOWN: A key for a pose in-between main poses, controlling the transition.
Keyframe.type.MOVING_HOLD: A key that is part of a held pose which still moves slightly.
Keyframe.type.EXTREME: An extreme pose or another special key you want to mark.
Keyframe.type.JITTER: A filler or baked key, made for keying on every frame.
Keyframe.type.GENERATED: A key made automatically by a tool, not by hand.
Keyframe.easing.AUTO: Blender picks the easing side automatically, based on the interpolation type.
Keyframe.easing.EASE_IN: Easing happens at the end closest to the next key.
Keyframe.easing.EASE_OUT: Easing happens at the end closest to this key.
Keyframe.easing.EASE_IN_OUT: Easing happens at both ends of the segment.

FCurve._: An F-Curve is the graph of one property over time, made from keyframes, that drives that property's animation.
FCurve.extrapolation: What the curve does before the first key and after the last key.
FCurve.data_path: The name of the property this curve animates, such as location.
FCurve.array_index: Which part of the property the curve controls: 0 is X, 1 is Y, 2 is Z (or R, G, B).
FCurve.color_mode: How the curve's color is chosen in the Graph Editor.
FCurve.color: The curve's color in the Graph Editor, used when Color Mode is Custom.
FCurve.select: Marks this curve as selected for editing.
FCurve.lock: Protects this curve from being edited by accident.
FCurve.mute: Turns the curve off, so it no longer changes the property.
FCurve.hide: Hides the curve and its keys in the Graph Editor. The animation still works.
FCurve.is_valid: Shows whether the curve could be used. It turns off if Blender failed to evaluate it, so it is skipped.
FCurve.extrapolation.CONSTANT: Holds the first or last key's value.
FCurve.extrapolation.LINEAR: Keeps going in a straight line using the slope at the end.
FCurve.color_mode.AUTO_RAINBOW: Cycles through rainbow colors so each curve looks different.
FCurve.color_mode.AUTO_RGB: Uses X red, Y green, Z blue for movement and color properties.
FCurve.color_mode.AUTO_YRGB: Uses W, X, Y, Z colors for rotation types with four values.
FCurve.color_mode.CUSTOM: Uses a color you pick by hand.
FCurve.auto_smoothing.NONE: Handles only look at the two nearest keys. Simple and quick.
FCurve.auto_smoothing.CONT_ACCEL: Handles are adjusted across the whole curve to avoid sudden jumps in speed.

Action._: An action stores a set of animation (curves and keyframes) that can be reused on an object.
Action.use_fake_user: Keeps this action in the file even if nothing uses it, so Blender does not delete it on save.
Action.use_extra_user: An internal flag saying an extra user holds this data. Mostly for developers, you can ignore it.
Action.is_runtime_data: Marks this data as temporary, so it will not be saved in the .blend file.
Action.tag: A hidden marker that tools use to flag data while they work. You do not need to touch it.
Action.use_frame_range: Lets you set the playback range of this action by hand instead of using the first and last keys.
Action.use_cyclic: Marks this action as a loop that repeats over its frame range, which helps tools that handle cycles.
Action.frame_start: First frame of the manually set playback range.
Action.frame_end: Last frame of the manually set playback range.
Action.frame_range: The playback range of this action. Uses the manual range if set, otherwise the range of its keyframes.

NlaStrip._: An NLA strip is a block of animation placed on a track, so you can layer, repeat and blend animations like video clips.
NlaStrip.extrapolation: What the strip does in gaps past its start and end.
NlaStrip.blend_type: How this strip combines with the animation below it.
NlaStrip.frame_start: The frame where the strip starts on the timeline.
NlaStrip.frame_end: The frame where the strip ends on the timeline.
NlaStrip.frame_start_raw: Start frame that accepts any number, even ones that overlap or break the strip. Mostly for scripts.
NlaStrip.frame_end_raw: End frame that accepts any number, even ones that overlap or break the strip. Mostly for scripts.
NlaStrip.frame_start_ui: Start frame as used in the interface. Changing it also adjusts the strip length so the action stays in place.
NlaStrip.frame_end_ui: End frame as used in the interface. Changing it also adjusts the strip length so the action stays in place.
NlaStrip.blend_in: Number of frames at the start where the strip fades in. 0 is an instant start, higher is a longer fade.
NlaStrip.blend_out: Number of frames at the end where the strip fades out. 0 is an instant stop, higher is a longer fade.
NlaStrip.use_auto_blend: Sets the fade in and out lengths automatically from where strips overlap.
NlaStrip.action_slot_handle: A number that says which part of the action this strip uses. Mostly for scripts.
NlaStrip.last_slot_identifier: The name of the action part most recently used by this strip. Mostly for scripts.
NlaStrip.action_frame_start: First frame of the action that the strip plays.
NlaStrip.action_frame_end: Last frame of the action that the strip plays.
NlaStrip.repeat: How many times the strip repeats its action. 1 plays once, 2 plays twice, and so on.
NlaStrip.scale: Speed scale of the action. Below 1 plays faster, above 1 plays slower.
NlaStrip.influence: How strongly the strip affects the result. 0 is none, 1 is full.
NlaStrip.strip_time: Which frame of the action is shown right now. Only used when strip time is animated.
NlaStrip.use_animated_influence: Lets an F-Curve control the strip's influence over time instead of fixed fades.
NlaStrip.use_animated_time: Lets an F-Curve control which action frame plays, so you can speed up, slow down or reverse.
NlaStrip.use_animated_time_cyclic: Loops the animated time within the action's start and end frames.
NlaStrip.mute: Turns the strip off so it does not affect the animation.
NlaStrip.use_reverse: Plays the strip backward. Only works when timing is automatic.
NlaStrip.use_sync_length: Updates the strip's action range after you edit its keyframes in tweak mode.
NlaStrip.extrapolation.NOTHING: The strip has no effect outside its own range.
NlaStrip.extrapolation.HOLD: Holds the first frame if there are no earlier strips, and holds the last frame after.
NlaStrip.extrapolation.HOLD_FORWARD: Only holds the last frame after the strip ends.
NlaStrip.blend_type.REPLACE: The strip's values replace what is below.
NlaStrip.blend_type.COMBINE: The strip's values are mixed in sensibly, such as adding movement and multiplying scale.
NlaStrip.blend_type.ADD: The strip's values are added on top of what is below.
NlaStrip.blend_type.SUBTRACT: The strip's values are subtracted from what is below.
NlaStrip.blend_type.MULTIPLY: The strip's values are multiplied with what is below.

AnimData._: The animation data block on an object, holding its active action, NLA tracks and drivers.
AnimData.action_extrapolation: What the active action does in gaps outside its range when using the NLA.
AnimData.action_blend_type: How the active action mixes with the NLA stack below it.
AnimData.action_influence: How strongly the active action affects the NLA result. 0 is none, 1 is full.
AnimData.action_slot_handle_tweak_storage: A place that temporarily holds the main action part while in tweak mode. For scripts.
AnimData.use_nla: Turns on the NLA stack so its strips are used for this object's animation.
AnimData.use_tweak_mode: Turns NLA tweak mode on or off, so you can edit a strip's action directly.
AnimData.use_pin: Keeps this animation visible in the Graph Editor even when the object is not selected.
AnimData.action_slot_handle: A number saying which part of the action this object uses. Mostly for scripts.
AnimData.last_slot_identifier: The name of the action part most recently used here. Mostly for scripts.
AnimData.action_extrapolation.NOTHING: The action has no effect outside its range.
AnimData.action_extrapolation.HOLD: Holds the first frame if no strips come before, and the last frame after.
AnimData.action_extrapolation.HOLD_FORWARD: Only holds the last frame after the action ends.
AnimData.action_blend_type.REPLACE: The action's values replace what the NLA stack gives.
AnimData.action_blend_type.COMBINE: The action's values are mixed in sensibly with the NLA result.
AnimData.action_blend_type.ADD: The action's values are added on top of the NLA result.
AnimData.action_blend_type.SUBTRACT: The action's values are subtracted from the NLA result.
AnimData.action_blend_type.MULTIPLY: The action's values are multiplied with the NLA result.

SpaceView3D._: Settings for a 3D Viewport: which panels and gizmos show, the camera lens, clipping, and which object types are visible or selectable.
SpaceView3D.show_locked_time: Keeps this editor's visible time range in step with other time-based editors, so they scroll together.
SpaceView3D.show_region_header: Shows or hides the header bar at the top of this editor.
SpaceView3D.show_region_tool_header: Shows or hides the strip under the header with options for the active tool.
SpaceView3D.show_region_toolbar: Shows or hides the toolbar of tools on the left side.
SpaceView3D.show_region_ui: Shows or hides the sidebar (N panel) on the right side.
SpaceView3D.show_region_hud: Shows or hides the small panel that lets you adjust the last operation you did.
SpaceView3D.show_region_asset_shelf: Shows or hides the shelf of assets (such as brushes) that fit your current mode.
SpaceView3D.use_render_border: Renders only a box inside the frame in the rendered viewport, which is faster to preview.
SpaceView3D.render_border_min_x: Left edge of the render box, from 0 (left) to 1 (right). Higher moves the left edge inward.
SpaceView3D.render_border_min_y: Bottom edge of the render box, from 0 (bottom) to 1 (top). Higher moves the bottom edge up.
SpaceView3D.render_border_max_x: Right edge of the render box, from 0 to 1. Lower moves the right edge inward.
SpaceView3D.render_border_max_y: Top edge of the render box, from 0 to 1. Lower moves the top edge down.
SpaceView3D.lock_bone: Keeps the view centered on this bone, following it as it moves.
SpaceView3D.lock_cursor: Keeps the view centered on the 3D cursor, following it as it moves.
SpaceView3D.lens: The viewport's zoom lens in millimeters. Low is wide and distorted, high is zoomed in and flat.
SpaceView3D.clip_start: Nearest distance you can see in the viewport. Things closer than this disappear. Too high cuts off near objects.
SpaceView3D.clip_end: Farthest distance you can see. Things farther than this disappear. Too low cuts off distant objects.
SpaceView3D.lock_camera: Lets you move the camera by navigating in camera view, as if the viewport were the camera.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo: Master switch that shows or hides all the on-screen handles (gizmos) in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_navigate: Shows the little navigation widget for rotating and zooming the view.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_context: Shows handles that depend on the selected item, such as a light or camera.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_modifier: Shows handles for the active modifier so you can adjust it in the viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_tool: Shows the handles of the active tool, such as the move arrows.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_object_translate: Shows the handle for moving the object.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_object_rotate: Shows the handle for rotating the object.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_object_scale: Shows the handle for scaling the object.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_empty_image: Shows the handle for resizing and positioning an image empty.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_empty_force_field: Shows the handle for adjusting a force field.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_light_size: Shows the handle for adjusting the size of spot and area lights.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_light_look_at: Shows the handle for aiming a light.
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_camera_lens: Shows the handle for adjusting a camera's zoom (focal length or orthographic scale).
SpaceView3D.show_gizmo_camera_dof_distance: Shows the handle for adjusting the camera's focus distance.
SpaceView3D.use_local_camera: Uses a camera chosen just for this viewport instead of the scene's active camera.
SpaceView3D.show_reconstruction: Shows 3D data rebuilt from a tracked movie clip.
SpaceView3D.tracks_display_size: Size of the tracked points shown in the viewport. Low is tiny, high is big.
SpaceView3D.tracks_display_type: Shape used to draw tracked points in the viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_camera_path: Shows the path the reconstructed camera moved along.
SpaceView3D.show_bundle_names: Shows the names of the tracked points in the viewport.
SpaceView3D.use_local_collections: Lets this viewport show its own set of collections, different from other viewports.
SpaceView3D.stereo_3d_camera: Which eye's view this viewport shows in stereo 3D.
SpaceView3D.show_stereo_3d_cameras: Shows the left and right cameras in the viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_stereo_3d_convergence_plane: Shows the plane where the two eyes' views meet (the screen depth).
SpaceView3D.stereo_3d_convergence_plane_alpha: See-through level of the convergence plane. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
SpaceView3D.show_stereo_3d_volume: Shows the pyramid-shaped volume each stereo camera sees.
SpaceView3D.stereo_3d_volume_alpha: See-through level of the camera volumes. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
SpaceView3D.mirror_xr_session: Makes this viewport show what the VR headset sees.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_mesh: Shows or hides mesh objects in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_curve: Shows or hides curve objects in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_surf: Shows or hides surface objects in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_meta: Shows or hides metaballs in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_font: Shows or hides text objects in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_curves: Shows or hides hair curves in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_pointcloud: Shows or hides point clouds in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_volume: Shows or hides volumes in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_armature: Shows or hides armatures (skeletons) in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_lattice: Shows or hides lattices in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_empty: Shows or hides empties in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_grease_pencil: Shows or hides Grease Pencil objects in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_camera: Shows or hides cameras in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_light: Shows or hides lights in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_speaker: Shows or hides speakers in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_viewport_light_probe: Shows or hides light probes in this viewport.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_mesh: Allows or blocks clicking to select mesh objects.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_curve: Allows or blocks clicking to select curve objects.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_surf: Allows or blocks clicking to select surface objects.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_meta: Allows or blocks clicking to select metaballs.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_font: Allows or blocks clicking to select text objects.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_curves: Allows or blocks clicking to select hair curves.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_pointcloud: Allows or blocks clicking to select point clouds.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_volume: Allows or blocks clicking to select volumes.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_armature: Allows or blocks clicking to select armatures.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_lattice: Allows or blocks clicking to select lattices.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_empty: Allows or blocks clicking to select empties.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_grease_pencil: Allows or blocks clicking to select Grease Pencil objects.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_camera: Allows or blocks clicking to select cameras.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_light: Allows or blocks clicking to select lights.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_speaker: Allows or blocks clicking to select speakers.
SpaceView3D.show_object_select_light_probe: Allows or blocks clicking to select light probes.
SpaceView3D.show_viewer: Shows the in-between geometry from Viewer nodes, so you can preview a step of a node setup.
SpaceView3D.tracks_display_type.PLAIN_AXES: Drawn as a small cross of three lines.
SpaceView3D.tracks_display_type.ARROWS: Drawn as three arrows pointing along the axes.
SpaceView3D.stereo_3d_camera.S3D: Shows both eyes combined as a 3D picture.

View3DOverlay._: Extra helper drawings laid over the 3D viewport, like the grid, outlines, origins, normals, statistics and paint-mode displays.
View3DOverlay.show_overlays: Master switch that shows or hides all overlays (grid, outlines, gizmo helpers) in this viewport.
View3DOverlay.show_ortho_grid: Shows the grid in side, front and top views.
View3DOverlay.show_floor: Shows the grid on the ground plane.
View3DOverlay.show_axis_x: Shows the red X axis line on the floor.
View3DOverlay.show_axis_y: Shows the green Y axis line on the floor.
View3DOverlay.show_axis_z: Shows the blue Z axis line (the vertical one).
View3DOverlay.grid_scale: Multiplier for the gap between grid lines. Below 1 packs lines tighter, above 1 spreads them out.
View3DOverlay.grid_lines: How many grid lines are drawn in perspective view. Low shows a small grid, high shows a larger one.
View3DOverlay.grid_subdivisions: How many small lines sit between the main grid lines. Low is simple, high is finer.
View3DOverlay.show_outline_selected: Draws an orange outline around selected objects.
View3DOverlay.show_object_origins: Shows the small dot marking the center (origin) of selected objects.
View3DOverlay.show_object_origins_all: Shows the origin dot for every object, not just selected ones.
View3DOverlay.show_relationship_lines: Shows dashed lines linking children to their parents and constraint targets.
View3DOverlay.show_cursor: Shows the 3D cursor in the viewport.
View3DOverlay.show_text: Shows text info such as the view name and object name in the corner.
View3DOverlay.show_stats: Shows scene statistics, like how many vertices, faces and objects there are.
View3DOverlay.show_performance: Shows how long the viewport takes to calculate and draw, to help find slow parts.
View3DOverlay.show_camera_guides: Shows composition guides inside the camera frame, such as the rule of thirds.
View3DOverlay.show_camera_passepartout: Darkens the area outside the camera frame so you see what the camera sees.
View3DOverlay.show_extras: Shows extra helper drawings like camera shapes, empties and light icons.
View3DOverlay.show_light_colors: Colors the light icons to match the light's color.
View3DOverlay.show_bones: Shows bones in the viewport. Turn off to see only the motion paths.
View3DOverlay.show_face_orientation: Colors faces blue if they face you and red if they face away. Useful for finding flipped faces.
View3DOverlay.show_fade_inactive: Fades out the objects you are not editing, so the active one stands out.
View3DOverlay.fade_inactive_alpha: How strongly inactive objects are faded. Low keeps them visible, high hides them more.
View3DOverlay.show_xray_bone: Shows bones through the mesh in X-Ray style, so you can select them.
View3DOverlay.xray_alpha_bone: How see-through bones appear. Low is faint, high is solid.
View3DOverlay.bone_wire_alpha: Highest opacity of bones in wireframe display. Low makes them faint, high makes them bold.
View3DOverlay.show_motion_paths: Shows the paths that moving objects and bones follow over time.
View3DOverlay.show_onion_skins: Shows ghost copies of earlier and later frames of the animation.
View3DOverlay.show_look_dev: Shows reference spheres (shiny and matte) that react to your lights, helping you judge lighting.
View3DOverlay.show_wireframes: Draws the edges of faces as wires over solid shading.
View3DOverlay.wireframe_threshold: Angle limit for showing wires. Low shows only sharp edges, 1 shows all edges.
View3DOverlay.wireframe_opacity: How solid the wires look. 0 is invisible, 1 is fully solid.
View3DOverlay.show_viewer_attribute: Shows the attribute colors from the active Viewer node on the mesh.
View3DOverlay.viewer_attribute_opacity: How strong the viewer attribute colors look. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
View3DOverlay.show_viewer_text: Shows the viewer attribute values as numbers in the viewport.
View3DOverlay.show_wpaint_contours: Shows contour lines through points that have the same weight, like height lines on a map.
View3DOverlay.show_weight: Shows weight colors in Edit Mode.
View3DOverlay.show_retopology: Hides the solid mesh and draws the edit mesh in front, so you can trace over a shape.
View3DOverlay.retopology_offset: How far the edit mesh is pulled toward you in retopology mode. Low sits close to the surface, high floats farther.
View3DOverlay.show_face_normals: Draws lines showing the direction each face points.
View3DOverlay.show_vertex_normals: Draws lines showing the direction each vertex points.
View3DOverlay.show_split_normals: Draws lines for custom normals, one for each corner of each face.
View3DOverlay.show_faces: Shows a colored tint on selected faces in Edit Mode.
View3DOverlay.show_face_center: Shows a dot at the center of each face in face select mode.
View3DOverlay.show_edge_crease: Shows crease marks that make edges sharper under Subdivision Surface.
View3DOverlay.show_edge_bevel_weight: Shows edge weights that control how much the Bevel modifier bevels.
View3DOverlay.show_edge_seams: Shows the seam lines that cut the mesh for UV unwrapping.
View3DOverlay.show_edge_sharp: Shows edges marked as sharp, used for shading and the Edge Split modifier.
View3DOverlay.show_freestyle_edge_marks: Shows edges marked for the Freestyle line renderer.
View3DOverlay.show_freestyle_face_marks: Shows faces marked for the Freestyle line renderer.
View3DOverlay.show_statvis: Colors the mesh to show problems like overhangs, thin areas or distortion.
View3DOverlay.show_extra_edge_length: Shows the length of selected edges as numbers.
View3DOverlay.show_extra_edge_angle: Shows the angle at selected edges as numbers.
View3DOverlay.show_extra_face_angle: Shows the corner angles of selected faces as numbers.
View3DOverlay.show_extra_face_area: Shows the area of selected faces as numbers.
View3DOverlay.show_extra_indices: Shows the index number of selected vertices, edges and faces.
View3DOverlay.display_handle: Which curve handles are drawn in Edit Mode.
View3DOverlay.show_curve_normals: Shows the direction lines of a 3D curve in Edit Mode.
View3DOverlay.normals_length: Length of the normal lines in the viewport. Low is short, high is long.
View3DOverlay.normals_constant_screen_size: Length of normal lines on screen when constant screen size is on. Low is short, high is long.
View3DOverlay.use_normals_constant_screen_size: Keeps normal lines the same size on screen however far you zoom.
View3DOverlay.texture_paint_mode_opacity: How strong the stencil mask looks in Texture Paint mode. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
View3DOverlay.vertex_paint_mode_opacity: How strong the stencil mask looks in Vertex Paint mode. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
View3DOverlay.weight_paint_mode_opacity: How strong the weight colors look in Weight Paint mode. 0 shows the mesh only, 1 shows only the colors.
View3DOverlay.sculpt_mode_mask_opacity: How dark masked areas look in Sculpt Mode. 0 shows no mask, 1 shows it fully.
View3DOverlay.show_sculpt_curves_cage: Shows the original hair curves you are editing as a cage.
View3DOverlay.sculpt_curves_cage_opacity: How strong the hair cage looks in curve sculpt mode. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
View3DOverlay.sculpt_mode_face_sets_opacity: How strong face set colors look in Sculpt Mode. 0 hides them, 1 shows them fully.
View3DOverlay.show_sculpt_mask: Shows the mask overlay in Sculpt Mode.
View3DOverlay.show_sculpt_face_sets: Shows the face set colors in Sculpt Mode.
View3DOverlay.show_annotation: Shows annotation drawings in this view.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_fade_objects: Fades all other objects so Grease Pencil drawings are easier to see.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_grid: Shows a grid over the Grease Pencil drawing area.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_fade_layers: Fades all Grease Pencil layers except the active one.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_fade_gp_objects: Fades Grease Pencil objects other than the active one.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_canvas_xray: Draws the canvas grid in front of everything.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_show_directions: Shows stroke direction: big green dot for the start and small red dot for the end.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_show_material_name: Shows the material name next to each stroke.
View3DOverlay.gpencil_grid_opacity: How solid the canvas grid looks. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
View3DOverlay.gpencil_grid_scale: Size of the canvas grid. Low makes small cells, high makes big ones.
View3DOverlay.gpencil_grid_offset: Moves the canvas grid sideways to line it up.
View3DOverlay.gpencil_grid_subdivisions: How many small lines sit inside each grid cell.
View3DOverlay.gpencil_fade_objects: How strongly other objects are faded. Low keeps them visible, high hides them.
View3DOverlay.gpencil_fade_layer: How strongly other layers are faded. Low keeps them visible, high hides them.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_edit_lines: Shows the connecting lines of strokes when editing them.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_multiedit_line_only: Shows edit lines only when you edit several frames at once.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_onion_skin: Shows ghost copies of the keyframes before and after the current one.
View3DOverlay.use_gpencil_onion_skin_active_object: Shows onion skins only for the active object.
View3DOverlay.vertex_opacity: How solid edit points look. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid.
View3DOverlay.gpencil_vertex_paint_opacity: How much the vertex paint colors mix into the stroke color. 0 shows none, 1 shows full color.
View3DOverlay.use_debug_freeze_view_culling: Debug option that freezes which objects are skipped as off-screen. Only for developers.
View3DOverlay.display_handle.SELECTED: Shows only handles of selected points.

View3DShading._: How objects look in the viewport: wireframe, solid, material preview or rendered, plus lighting, color and X-Ray options.
View3DShading.type: The main style the 3D viewport uses to draw your scene.
View3DShading.light: The lighting style in Solid mode.
View3DShading.show_object_outline: Draws a dark outline around objects to separate them from the background.
View3DShading.studio_light: Which studio lighting setup is used in Solid mode.
View3DShading.use_world_space_lighting: Makes the lighting fixed in the scene, instead of following the camera as you orbit.
View3DShading.show_backface_culling: Hides the back side of faces, so you only see faces looking at you.
View3DShading.show_cavity: Adds shading to dents and ridges to bring out surface detail.
View3DShading.cavity_type: How the cavity shading is calculated.
View3DShading.curvature_ridge_factor: Strength of the light edges on ridges (screen cavity). 0 is none, higher is stronger.
View3DShading.curvature_valley_factor: Strength of the dark lines in valleys (screen cavity). 0 is none, higher is stronger.
View3DShading.cavity_ridge_factor: Strength of lighting on ridges (world cavity). 0 is none, higher is stronger.
View3DShading.cavity_valley_factor: Strength of darkening in valleys (world cavity). 0 is none, higher is stronger.
View3DShading.studiolight_rotate_z: Turns the studio light around the up axis. Moves where highlights and shadows fall.
View3DShading.studiolight_intensity: Brightness of the studio light. Low is dim, high is bright.
View3DShading.studiolight_background_alpha: How visible the lighting image is in the background. 0 is hidden, 1 is fully shown.
View3DShading.studiolight_background_blur: How blurry the lighting image is in the background. 0 is sharp, higher is blurrier.
View3DShading.use_studiolight_view_rotation: Makes the lighting image fixed in the scene instead of turning with your view.
View3DShading.color_type: What color is used to draw objects in Solid mode.
View3DShading.wireframe_color_type: What color the wires are drawn in.
View3DShading.single_color: The color used when Color is set to Single.
View3DShading.background_color: The color used when Background is set to Viewport.
View3DShading.show_xray: Makes the whole scene see-through so you can see behind objects.
View3DShading.xray_alpha: How see-through objects are in X-Ray. 0 is fully clear, 1 is solid.
View3DShading.xray_alpha_wireframe: How see-through objects are in wireframe X-Ray. 0 is fully clear, 1 is solid.
View3DShading.use_dof: Blurs the background using the active camera's depth of field settings.
View3DShading.use_scene_lights: Uses the lights in your scene to light the viewport.
View3DShading.use_scene_world: Uses the scene's world for lighting.
View3DShading.use_scene_lights_render: Uses the lights in your scene in the rendered viewport.
View3DShading.use_scene_world_render: Uses the scene's world for lighting in the rendered viewport.
View3DShading.object_outline_color: The color of the outline around objects.
View3DShading.shadow_intensity: How dark shadows are. 0 is no shadow, 1 is very dark.
View3DShading.render_pass: Which render pass (layer of the image data) the viewport shows.
View3DShading.aov_name: The name of the custom shader output (AOV) to show.
View3DShading.use_compositor: When the compositor effects are shown in the viewport.
View3DShading.type.WIREFRAME: Shows only the edges of objects, with no surfaces. Fast and see-through.
View3DShading.type.SOLID: Shows objects as plain surfaces with simple lighting. Fast and clear for modeling.
View3DShading.type.MATERIAL: Previews your materials using a built-in environment and lights. Good for quick look checks.
View3DShading.type.RENDERED: Previews the final image using the active render engine. Most accurate, but slowest.
View3DShading.light.STUDIO: Lights the object like a photo studio.
View3DShading.light.MATCAP: Lights with a MatCap, a ball image that fakes lighting and material on the surface.
View3DShading.light.FLAT: No lighting at all, just flat color. Good for seeing pure colors.
View3DShading.cavity_type.WORLD: Based on the 3D surface in the scene. Good for large shapes and details.
View3DShading.cavity_type.SCREEN: Based on curvature as seen on screen. Good for fine details and sharp edges.
View3DShading.color_type.MATERIAL: Uses the viewport color of each material.
View3DShading.color_type.OBJECT: Uses the color set on each object.
View3DShading.color_type.RANDOM: Gives each object a random color, to tell them apart.
View3DShading.color_type.VERTEX: Shows the active vertex color layer.
View3DShading.color_type.TEXTURE: Shows the texture of the active image texture node.
View3DShading.color_type.SINGLE: Paints the whole scene in one color you pick.
View3DShading.wireframe_color_type.THEME: Uses the wire color from your theme.
View3DShading.wireframe_color_type.RANDOM: Gives each object a random wire color.
View3DShading.background_type.THEME: Uses the background color from your theme.
View3DShading.background_type.WORLD: Uses the world's background color from your scene.
View3DShading.background_type.VIEWPORT: Uses your own color just for this viewport.
View3DShading.render_pass.COMBINED: The full final image with everything together.
View3DShading.render_pass.EMISSION: Only light that surfaces give off themselves.
View3DShading.render_pass.ENVIRONMENT: Only the background and world lighting.
View3DShading.render_pass.AO: Ambient occlusion: darkening in tight corners and creases.
View3DShading.render_pass.DIFFUSE_COLOR: Only the base color of surfaces, without lighting.
View3DShading.render_pass.SPECULAR_LIGHT: Only the shiny highlights and reflections lighting.
View3DShading.render_pass.SPECULAR_COLOR: Only the color of the shiny reflections.
View3DShading.render_pass.VOLUME_LIGHT: Only light that passes through fog or smoke.
View3DShading.render_pass.POSITION: Where each pixel is in 3D space, shown as color.
View3DShading.render_pass.NORMAL: Which way each surface points, shown as color.
View3DShading.render_pass.MIST: How far things are, fading into mist.
View3DShading.render_pass.CryptoObject: A color-coded mask of each object, used for selecting objects in compositing.

Strip._: A strip is one clip, image, sound or effect on the Video Sequencer timeline.
Strip.select_left_handle: Marks the strip's left handle as selected.
Strip.select_right_handle: Marks the strip's right handle as selected.
Strip.mute: Turns the strip off so it adds nothing to the output.
Strip.lock: Locks the strip so it cannot be moved or changed by accident.
Strip.frame_final_duration: How long the strip plays in frames, after trimming the handles.
Strip.duration: Total length of the strip in frames, from the left handle to the right handle.
Strip.frame_start: The frame where the strip begins on the timeline. Changing it moves the whole strip.
Strip.content_start: The timeline frame where the original clip starts.
Strip.frame_final_start: First frame shown after trimming. Changing it trims the start of the strip.
Strip.left_handle: Timeline frame of the left handle, which is where the strip starts.
Strip.frame_final_end: Last frame shown after trimming. Changing it trims the end of the strip.
Strip.right_handle: Timeline frame of the right handle, the first frame where the strip no longer plays.
Strip.frame_offset_start: How many frames are cut from the start of the clip. Higher trims more.
Strip.left_handle_offset: How far the left handle sits to the right of the clip's start.
Strip.frame_offset_end: How many frames are cut from the end of the clip. Higher trims more.
Strip.right_handle_offset: How far the right handle sits to the left of the clip's end.
Strip.channel: Which row (layer) the strip sits on. Higher channels draw above lower ones.
Strip.blend_type: How the strip's picture mixes with the strips below it.
Strip.blend_alpha: How strongly the strip shows over others. 0 is invisible, 1 is fully visible.
Strip.effect_fader: Manual fade position of an effect or transition. 0 is start, 1 is end.
Strip.use_default_fade: Uses the built-in fade, which usually lasts as long as the effect strip.
Strip.color_tag: A color label to help you organize strips. It does not change the video.
Strip.show_retiming_keys: Shows retiming keys on the strip so you can move them to change speed.
Strip.blend_type.CROSS: Fades between this strip and those below.
Strip.blend_type.MULTIPLY: Multiplies colors, making the result darker.
Strip.blend_type.LINEAR_BURN: Darkens strongly by adding colors and subtracting white.
Strip.blend_type.SCREEN: Lightens the picture, like projecting two images together.
Strip.blend_type.ADD: Adds the colors together, making things brighter.
Strip.blend_type.OVERLAY: Boosts contrast: darks get darker and lights get lighter.
Strip.blend_type.VIVID_LIGHT: A very strong contrast and color boost.
Strip.blend_type.LINEAR_LIGHT: A strong light effect that brightens or darkens.
Strip.blend_type.PIN_LIGHT: Replaces colors depending on brightness, for a patchy look.
Strip.blend_type.DIFFERENCE: Shows the gap between colors, giving inverted odd colors.
Strip.blend_type.EXCLUSION: Like Difference but softer, with lower contrast.
Strip.blend_type.SUBTRACT: Subtracts this strip's colors from the ones below.
Strip.blend_type.HUE: Takes only the hue (color type) from this strip.
Strip.blend_type.SATURATION: Takes only the color strength from this strip.
Strip.blend_type.COLOR: Takes hue and saturation from this strip, keeping the brightness below.
Strip.blend_type.VALUE: Takes only the brightness from this strip.
Strip.blend_type.ALPHA_OVER: Puts this strip over the ones below, using transparency.
Strip.blend_type.ALPHA_UNDER: Puts this strip under the ones below, using transparency.
Strip.blend_type.GAMMA_CROSS: Fades between strips with a gamma correction, which looks more natural.
